arxiv:2605.05639|f789c55ed021f425ce20d41.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型推理中由 KV cache 带来的带宽与容量瓶颈，提出了一种面向 KV 中心服务的异构 HBM-PIM 架构与运行时。该方案利用 HBM4 逻辑 die 作为层内控制点，将堆栈划分为密集存储层与支持近存计算的 PIM 计算层，以减少不必要的逻辑开销并提升资源利用率。系统在硬件层面支持跨层 DMA、分层地址转换、注意力相关的数据聚合/广播以及迁移过程中的在线量化。基于真实轨迹评估结果表明，该设计可显著提升 token 吞吐、服务容量，并降低每 token 能耗。
arxiv:2605.05639|f789c55ed021f425ce20d41.tldr: TokenStack 通过异构 HBM-PIM 与层内运行时协同优化 LLM 推理中的 KV cache 访问，显著提升吞吐和能效。
arxiv:2605.05639|f789c55ed021f425ce20d41.recommendation_reason: 该研究聚焦于大语言模型推理加速、KV cache 访问优化、HBM-PIM 架构设计以及近存计算与运行时协同管理，与关注模型推理系统、存储层次优化和硬件加速方向的研究主题高度相关。

arxiv:2605.06485|c71d18f20e6ca8c35db5f8c.summary_zh: 本文提出了一种面向消费级 CPU 的三值神经网络推理方案，通过自定义 SIMD 内核将矩阵乘法替换为加减运算，以更好利用现代处理器的整数点积指令。作者实现了可直接通过 pip 安装的 Litespark-Inference，并与 Hugging Face 生态集成，便于实际部署。实验结果表明，该方法在 Apple Silicon 上相比标准 PyTorch 推理显著提升了首 token 生成速度、整体吞吐量，并降低了内存占用。该工作展示了在缺少昂贵 GPU 的情况下，将高效模型推理下沉到个人电脑上的可行性。
arxiv:2605.06485|c71d18f20e6ca8c35db5f8c.tldr: 本文用自定义 SIMD 内核加速三值神经网络推理，使消费级 CPU 上的大模型推理更快、更省内存。
arxiv:2605.06485|c71d18f20e6ca8c35db5f8c.recommendation_reason: 该研究聚焦于高效模型推理、CPU 端加速和神经网络量化/低精度计算，与关注模型部署效率、推理优化和资源受限环境下 AI 计算的主题高度相关。

arxiv:2605.05819|4d7895a62eb5f62600711fd.summary_zh: 该研究针对资源受限设备上大模型推理时的显存不足和性能瓶颈问题，提出了一种基于误差补偿的异构推理系统 HCInfer。方法将压缩后的主干模型部署在 GPU 上执行，同时把残差补偿部分卸载到 CPU，以降低显存压力并保持推理效率。系统还设计了异步补偿流水线和面向敏感度的动态秩分配机制，用于进一步隐藏补偿开销并提升精度恢复效果。实验结果表明，该方法在下游任务上可带来最高 5.2% 的准确率提升，并相较于全精度模型实现最高 10.4 倍加速。
arxiv:2605.05819|4d7895a62eb5f62600711fd.tldr: HCInfer 通过将误差补偿部分卸载到 CPU 并结合异步流水线与动态秩分配，实现了资源受限设备上的高效大模型推理。
arxiv:2605.05819|4d7895a62eb5f62600711fd.recommendation_reason: 该论文与大模型高效推理、模型压缩后精度恢复、异构计算卸载以及面向资源受限设备的系统优化等研究主题高度相关。

arxiv:2605.06221|006d9211acfe058173cd1a3.summary_zh: 本文提出了 UniPrefill，一种面向长上下文预填充阶段的通用加速框架，旨在降低大语言模型在长文本推理中的计算开销。该方法不局限于稀疏注意力，而是从 token 级别直接加速计算，因此能够适配多种模型架构，包括混合注意力结构。作者还将其实现为连续批处理算子，并对 vLLM 的调度策略进行扩展，使其能够更自然地支持预填充与解码协同处理。实验表明，UniPrefill 在 TTFT 上最高可实现 2.1 倍加速，且在并发请求增多时收益更明显。
arxiv:2605.06221|006d9211acfe058173cd1a3.tldr: UniPrefill 通过通用的 token 级动态稀疏化实现长上下文预填充加速，并可无缝集成到 vLLM 等推理系统中。
arxiv:2605.06221|006d9211acfe058173cd1a3.recommendation_reason: 该研究聚焦于长上下文推理加速、稀疏化计算与大模型推理系统优化，与高效注意力机制、长文本处理和推理加速方向具有较强主题相似性。

arxiv:2605.05971|3e3dd56aae08c349a1d559c.summary_zh: 这篇论文聚焦于长上下文语言模型中的 KV cache 内存与解码开销问题，指出现有后验压缩方法的效果受限于模型内部表征本身的可压缩性。作者从理论上定义并分析了 KV 可压缩性，证明相同的序列到向量函数可以由可压缩或不可压缩的 Transformer 实现。基于这一认识，论文提出了 KV-Compression Aware Training（KV-CAT）继续预训练方法，通过训练时的 KV 稀疏化策略促使模型学习更易压缩的表征。实验表明，该方法能在检索、长上下文问答和压缩前缀续写等任务上改善压缩质量与性能开销之间的平衡。
arxiv:2605.05971|3e3dd56aae08c349a1d559c.tldr: 通过在训练阶段引导 Transformer 学习更易压缩的 KV 表征，提升长上下文模型的缓存压缩效果与实用性。
arxiv:2605.05971|3e3dd56aae08c349a1d559c.recommendation_reason: 该研究与长上下文建模、注意力缓存压缩、Transformer 表征学习以及大模型推理效率优化等主题高度相关，适合关注模型压缩和高效推理方法的读者。

arxiv:2605.06046|227ff12c3f30ddc31cb49d0.summary_zh: 这篇论文研究了大语言模型推理阶段的批处理调度问题，重点分析了批大小与前缀同质性之间的权衡。作者指出，在具有前缀共享的请求负载下，较小但前缀一致的批次可能比更大的异构批次具有更高的解码吞吐量，因为它们能带来更好的 KV cache 访问局部性。为此，论文提出了基于强化学习的调度器 Feather，用于学习最优的批次选择策略，并引入轻量级数据结构 Chunked Hash Tree 来降低前缀检测开销。实验结果表明，Feather 在多种场景下都能显著提升端到端吞吐量，同时在缺乏前缀共享时不会劣于现有方法。
arxiv:2605.06046|227ff12c3f30ddc31cb49d0.tldr: 论文提出一种面向前缀共享请求的 RL 调度器，通过平衡批大小与前缀同质性来提升 LLM 推理吞吐量。
arxiv:2605.06046|227ff12c3f30ddc31cb49d0.recommendation_reason: 该研究聚焦于大语言模型推理加速、批处理调度、KV cache 访问优化以及前缀共享工作负载管理，与关注模型推理系统性能提升和请求调度优化的研究主题高度相关。

arxiv:2605.05899|f8fbe1a31e77a653a727c5d.summary_zh: 该论文面向内存受限平台上的视觉-语言 MoE 模型部署问题，关注如何提升推理效率。作者指出，视觉输入会带来更大且更不稳定的专家访问模式，使现有主要针对文本场景的 MoE offloading 方法效果下降。为此，论文提出 VisMMoE，通过剪枝冗余视觉 token、预测专家访问并协同缓存与流水线调度，来缩小并稳定专家工作集。实验表明，该方法在保持具有竞争力精度的同时，显著提升了端到端推理性能。
arxiv:2605.05899|f8fbe1a31e77a653a727c5d.tldr: VisMMoE 通过视觉 token 压缩与专家访问预测，提升了视觉-语言 MoE 在低内存环境下的推理效率。
arxiv:2605.05899|f8fbe1a31e77a653a727c5d.recommendation_reason: 该研究聚焦于大规模 MoE 模型的高效部署、专家访问模式优化以及资源受限条件下的推理加速，与视觉-语言模型系统优化和模型卸载调度等方向具有较强主题相似性。

arxiv:2605.05219|09c8b1790d1e481d04ecf68.summary_zh: 本文研究了面向混合式和循环式大语言模型服务的前缀缓存优化问题。与传统依赖稠密 token 级 KV 复用的方法不同，作者针对状态空间模型和循环层提出在稀疏检查点位置保存精确状态，并从最近的检查点恢复后重算剩余后缀。该方法被形式化为在重叠深度分布下的检查点放置问题，并给出了一个精确的动态规划求解方案。实验表明，在多个真实数据集上，该方法在固定预算下能够更好地平衡延迟与缓存开销，并在低检查点预算时优势尤为明显。
arxiv:2605.05219|09c8b1790d1e481d04ecf68.tldr: 本文提出一种面向循环/混合 LLM 的稀疏前缀缓存方法，通过分布感知的检查点放置在保持精确输出的同时提升服务效率。
arxiv:2605.05219|09c8b1790d1e481d04ecf68.recommendation_reason: 该研究与前缀缓存、推理加速、LLM 服务优化以及循环或状态空间模型的缓存复用问题高度相关，关注点与检索到的相关工作在模型状态复用和延迟优化方面一致。

arxiv:2605.06554|21b72fc17f73c3591c1f2ef.summary_zh: 本文提出了一种用于超长序列预训练的训练期注意力方法 Lighthouse Attention，用于缓解标准缩放点积注意力在时间和显存上的二次方瓶颈。该方法通过分层的选择式压缩与解压缩，对序列进行自适应处理，并且在压缩过程中同时处理 query、key 和 value，以保持因果顺序并提升并行性。由于其选择过程是无梯度的，因此避免了复杂且可能低效的反向传播实现。作者还设计了两阶段训练流程：前期大部分时间使用 Lighthouse Attention 预训练，后期切换回完整注意力进行短暂恢复训练。小规模实验表明，该方法在匹配其他设置时可加快总训练时间并获得更低的最终损失。
arxiv:2605.06554|21b72fc17f73c3591c1f2ef.tldr: 该工作提出一种可在训练阶段替代标准注意力的分层压缩方法，以更高效地进行长上下文预训练并在末期恢复为完整注意力模型。
arxiv:2605.06554|21b72fc17f73c3591c1f2ef.recommendation_reason: 该论文与长上下文建模、注意力机制优化、Transformer 训练效率提升以及大模型预训练加速等研究主题高度相关。

arxiv:2605.05838|c93eb9b37d5c47bb08a0d9d.summary_zh: 本文提出了 Momentum DeltaNet（MDN），旨在提升线性注意力模型在长序列建模中的训练效率与效果。作者将线性注意力中的递推更新重解释为带动量的分块并行优化过程，并通过几何重排实现 stepwise momentum 的并行化。论文还从动力系统角度分析了该递推的稳定性，并据此设计了门控约束以增强训练稳定性。实验表明，MDN 在保持较高训练吞吐的同时，在多个基准上优于或接近强线性模型及 Transformer 基线。
arxiv:2605.05838|c93eb9b37d5c47bb08a0d9d.tldr: MDN 通过并行化 stepwise momentum 改进线性注意力模型的长序列训练效率与性能。
arxiv:2605.05838|c93eb9b37d5c47bb08a0d9d.recommendation_reason: 该研究聚焦于线性注意力、长序列建模和高效训练优化，与关注高效序列模型、状态空间模型或注意力机制改进的研究主题高度相似。

arxiv:2605.05628|b9b848bcf16b67b3963cc82.summary_zh: 本文针对多GPU系统中大语言模型张量并行带来的高频集合通信开销，指出现有in-switch computing方案虽然能减少冗余数据传输，但其通信导向设计与LLM计算内核的内存语义存在不匹配。为此，作者提出了首个面向计算感知的in-switch computing框架CAIS，通过计算感知的ISA与微架构扩展、融合感知的TB协调以及图级数据流优化来提升通信与计算的协同效率。实验结果表明，CAIS能够在LLM工作负载上实现更紧密的跨内核重叠，并显著提升端到端训练速度。该方法在多GPU张量并行加速方面展示了较强的实用价值。
arxiv:2605.05628|b9b848bcf16b67b3963cc82.tldr: CAIS通过让in-switch computing更贴合LLM计算语义，显著提升了多GPU张量并行的通信-计算重叠与训练性能。
arxiv:2605.05628|b9b848bcf16b67b3963cc82.recommendation_reason: 该研究主题与多GPU系统中的大模型张量并行、集合通信优化、通信计算重叠以及面向LLM的系统加速密切相关，适合关注分布式深度学习性能优化与智能网卡/交换机计算协同设计的读者。

arxiv:2605.05222|850a4b0515d533be68f17c3.summary_zh: 本文提出了一种面向 Transformer 的按 token 自适应计算深度方法，通过在相邻层之间为每个 token 学习门控，决定是否跳过残差更新。该机制使用轻量级两层 MLP 生成连续的停止概率，能够端到端训练，并且只带来约 1.7% 的参数开销。实验表明，即使没有显式深度正则，模型也能根据任务损失自动学习到难度相关的路由策略。作者在字符级语言建模任务上实现了 14% 到 23% 的 token-层操作节省，同时几乎不损失性能，并可直接用于推理阶段的稀疏执行加速。
arxiv:2605.05222|850a4b0515d533be68f17c3.tldr: 通过学习每个 token 的动态路由与跳层决策，Transformer 可以在几乎不损失精度的情况下显著减少计算量。
arxiv:2605.05222|850a4b0515d533be68f17c3.recommendation_reason: 该研究与自适应计算、动态推理、Transformer 稀疏化和基于 token 的计算分配等主题高度相关，适合关注模型效率优化和条件计算机制的读者。

arxiv:2605.06105|b9f9d4c3b4dfa64b99b44a1.summary_zh: 本文提出了一种用于长上下文推理的阶段不对称 KV 可见性策略 SPEED，通过让预填充阶段的提示 token 只在较浅层保留 KV，而在解码阶段保持 token 的全层深度可见，从而降低长上下文推理成本。该方法以极少的 BoS 锚点维持整体性能，并避免上层层级中预填充 token 的无谓缓存与注意力开销。在 Llama-3.1-8B 的指令微调实验中，SPEED 在只使用 75% 层进行预填充时，仍保持与全深度基线接近的效果。实验结果表明，该策略可显著改善 TTFT、TPOT 和显存占用，适合高效长上下文推理场景。
arxiv:2605.06105|b9f9d4c3b4dfa64b99b44a1.tldr: SPEED 通过让长提示在预填充阶段只保留浅层 KV、解码阶段保持全深度可见，实现了长上下文推理的高效加速且几乎不损失效果。
arxiv:2605.06105|b9f9d4c3b4dfa64b99b44a1.recommendation_reason: 该研究聚焦于长上下文推理效率优化、KV 缓存压缩以及分层注意力可见性控制，与长文本建模和高效大模型推理方向高度相关。

arxiv:2605.06546|e2ca30e9bd99cf1b0fb8c17.summary_zh: 本文提出了一种名为 Token-Superposition Training（TST）的预训练方法，通过将多个连续 token 合并为一个“袋”并使用多热交叉熵目标进行训练，从而提升单位 FLOPs 下的数据吞吐效率。该方法不需要修改并行策略、优化器、分词器、数据或模型结构，属于可直接插入式的训练改进方案。TST 采用“超位置训练 + 恢复训练”两阶段流程，在多个参数规模上都表现出较强鲁棒性。实验结果表明，TST 在基线损失和下游任务上均有提升，并且在等损失条件下可显著缩短预训练时间。
arxiv:2605.06546|e2ca30e9bd99cf1b0fb8c17.tldr: TST 通过将多个 token 合并训练，在不改模型结构的前提下显著提升大模型预训练效率。
arxiv:2605.06546|e2ca30e9bd99cf1b0fb8c17.recommendation_reason: 该工作与高效大模型预训练、训练加速、数据吞吐优化以及降低预训练计算成本等研究主题高度相关。

arxiv:2605.06206|76521fbce245ba3f1e9ffed.summary_zh: 本文提出了一种面向大语言模型分布式推理的 Federation of Experts（FoE）架构，旨在缓解混合专家模型在分布式场景中的通信瓶颈。FoE 将 Transformer 层中的 MoE 模块重构为多个 MoE 集群，使专家并行与通信范围更局部化，从而减少跨设备、跨节点的数据传输。在单节点场景下，FoE 可完全消除 all-to-all 通信；在多节点场景下，则将该通信限制在节点内部网络中。实验结果表明，FoE 在保持与同规模 MoE 模型相近生成质量的同时，显著提升了推理吞吐量并降低了延迟。
arxiv:2605.06206|76521fbce245ba3f1e9ffed.tldr: FoE 通过重构 MoE 结构显著降低了大模型分布式推理中的通信开销，并提升了推理效率。
arxiv:2605.06206|76521fbce245ba3f1e9ffed.recommendation_reason: 该研究与分布式大模型推理、混合专家结构优化以及通信效率提升等主题高度相关，适合关注模型部署性能和系统加速方法的读者。

arxiv:2605.05741|de79bfb72aa2762d0ccaf4d.summary_zh: 本文提出 HyperLens，一种用于追踪大语言模型推理过程中细粒度置信度轨迹的高分辨率探针。作者指出 Transformer 深层具有放大层间置信度微小变化的机制，从而可以更精细地刻画模型的推理动态。基于这一观察，论文构建了一个量化“认知努力”的指标，并在多种模型和数据集上验证了复杂任务通常对应更高的认知努力。研究还发现，标准监督微调可能降低认知努力，进而导致部分任务性能下降。
arxiv:2605.05741|de79bfb72aa2762d0ccaf4d.tldr: HyperLens 通过细粒度置信度轨迹量化大语言模型的认知努力，并揭示复杂任务需要更高的推理投入。
arxiv:2605.05741|de79bfb72aa2762d0ccaf4d.recommendation_reason: 该研究聚焦于大语言模型的推理动态、置信度演化以及复杂度与模型内部计算行为之间的关系，与研究模型可解释性、推理过程分析和性能退化机制的主题高度相关。

arxiv:2605.06116|612957243de78330947c023.summary_zh: 本文研究了在推理阶段如何通过逐步路由不同规模的语言模型来降低大模型推理成本，同时尽量保持推理性能。作者将逐步模型路由建模为一个受约束的决策问题，并使用强化学习训练一个小型控制策略。该方法结合阈值校准来调整性能与效率之间的权衡。实验在 GSM8K、MATH500 和 OmniMath 等数学基准上验证了方法有效性，结果显示其在准确率与成本的折中上优于手工路由策略，并接近依赖大型过程奖励模型的方法。
arxiv:2605.06116|612957243de78330947c023.tldr: 本文通过强化学习训练小型控制策略，实现了更低成本的逐步模型路由，并显著改善了准确率与推理开销的权衡。
arxiv:2605.06116|612957243de78330947c023.recommendation_reason: 该研究与推理时模型选择、成本敏感推理、路由策略优化以及大语言模型在复杂推理任务中的效率提升等主题高度相关。

arxiv:2605.06402|2e2eb5323912a027f9f3fd8.summary_zh: SparseForge提出了一种用于大语言模型半结构化稀疏化的后训练框架，重点不是增加重训练规模，而是直接优化稀疏掩码以提升恢复效率。该方法结合 Hessian 感知的重要性估计与软掩码的渐进退火，将稀疏模式稳定地收敛到可由硬件执行的结构化稀疏形式。实验表明，在 2:4 稀疏下，它只用较少的重训练 token 就能获得接近甚至超过稠密模型的零样本性能。结果还显示，这种精度与效率的平衡优势在不同模型家族中具有一致性。
arxiv:2605.06402|2e2eb5323912a027f9f3fd8.tldr: SparseForge 通过 Hessian 引导的软掩码退火实现高效的半结构化 LLM 稀疏化，并以较低重训练成本恢复模型精度。
arxiv:2605.06402|2e2eb5323912a027f9f3fd8.recommendation_reason: 该研究与大语言模型压缩、后训练剪枝、结构化稀疏化以及稀疏恢复效率优化等方向高度相关。

arxiv:2605.06501|f4cfccb9c1907e3be5bf669.summary_zh: 本文提出了一种基于核岭回归（KRR）的新型 token mixing 结构 Cubit，用来替代 Transformer 中传统的注意力机制。作者从理论上将注意力解释为 Nadaraya-Watson 回归，并进一步引入 KRR 的闭式解来增强 token 间信息聚合能力。为提升训练稳定性，论文还提出了 Limited-Range Rescale（LRR）对 value 层进行受控缩放。实验结果表明，Cubit 在长序列建模任务上可能具有更强的表现，且随着训练序列长度增加，其相对优势更明显。
arxiv:2605.06501|f4cfccb9c1907e3be5bf669.tldr: Cubit 用核岭回归重构 Transformer 的 token 混合机制，并在长序列建模上表现出更强潜力。
arxiv:2605.06501|f4cfccb9c1907e3be5bf669.recommendation_reason: 该研究与基于 Transformer 的序列建模、注意力机制改进以及长上下文建模方法高度相关，特别适合关注 token 混合机制优化和替代注意力架构的研究方向。

arxiv:2605.05888|5af5a7778c968c08c992454.summary_zh: 本文针对多 GPU 系统中 MoE 模型的通信瓶颈，指出其根源在于动态的专家路由与 GPU 静态、以地址为中心的通信模型之间存在抽象不匹配。为解决这一问题，作者提出了 MoE-Hub，一种软硬件协同设计的方法，通过目的地无关的通信范式将数据传输与地址管理解耦。系统中由轻量级硬件在 GPU hub 中透明处理地址分配与数据流编排，从而降低软件复杂度并实现通信与计算的无缝重叠。实验结果表明，该方法在单层和端到端场景下均带来了显著性能提升。
arxiv:2605.05888|5af5a7778c968c08c992454.tldr: MoE-Hub 通过硬件加速通信控制平面，缓解多 GPU MoE 的通信瓶颈并实现计算通信重叠。
arxiv:2605.05888|5af5a7778c968c08c992454.recommendation_reason: 研究主题与多 GPU 系统上的通信优化、计算与通信重叠、以及面向高性能 AI 模型的软硬件协同设计高度相关，适合关注分布式深度学习加速与体系结构优化的读者。

arxiv:2605.06676|b7bb7dda601805313426fa0.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型长上下文推理中 KV cache 随序列长度线性增长、占用内存巨大的问题，提出了端到端可学习的 LKV 方法。该方法将 KV 压缩建模为可微分优化问题，分别通过学习头级预算分配和 token 重要性选择来替代传统启发式策略。与依赖统计先验或固定归纳偏置的方法相比，LKV 能更紧密地对齐任务目标，从而减少资源误配。实验表明，在 LongBench 和 RULER 上，LKV 在高压缩率下仍能保持优异性能，且仅保留 15% KV cache 也可接近无损。
arxiv:2605.06676|b7bb7dda601805313426fa0.tldr: LKV 通过端到端学习 KV cache 的预算分配与 token 选择，在大幅压缩下仍保持长上下文推理性能。
arxiv:2605.06676|b7bb7dda601805313426fa0.recommendation_reason: 该研究聚焦于大语言模型长上下文推理中的 KV cache 压缩与 eviction，与需要提升推理效率、降低显存占用的相关研究主题高度相似。

arxiv:2605.07234|6d6f4627cb3cb80be6e49ef.summary_zh: 本文针对长上下文大语言模型推理中的 KV Cache 膨胀问题，重新定义了缓存淘汰任务。作者指出，现有方法主要依赖局部注意力权重，未充分考虑 value 表示、输出投影以及多头之间的相互作用。为此，论文提出 LaProx，将淘汰问题建模为输出感知的、按层进行的矩阵乘法近似问题，并据此为 token 计算全局可比的重要性分数。实验表明，该方法在仅保留 5% KV Cache 的情况下仍能维持较好的模型性能，并在多个长上下文基准上优于现有方法。
arxiv:2605.07234|6d6f4627cb3cb80be6e49ef.tldr: 这项工作提出了一种更全面的 KV Cache 淘汰方法，在极低缓存占用下仍能有效保持长上下文推理性能。
arxiv:2605.07234|6d6f4627cb3cb80be6e49ef.recommendation_reason: 该研究聚焦于长上下文大语言模型推理中的缓存压缩、记忆管理与高效推理，与关注模型长文本处理和资源优化的研究主题高度相关。

arxiv:2605.07719|f8405365322adb21f0353d4.summary_zh: 本文针对长上下文推理中 KV cache 常驻 CPU 内存所带来的性能瓶颈，提出了一种结合稀疏注意力与 CPU-GPU 并行的高效混合方案。该方法通过输出感知的 KV 预算分配、面向不同注意力头与粒度的稀疏配置，以及跨设备协同执行来提升整体效率。系统中还引入了轻量级头属性预测器、预算选择器和优先级调度器，以联合优化精度与吞吐。实验表明，该方法在多模型、多基准和多任务上能够较好保持质量，并显著加速推理。
arxiv:2605.07719|f8405365322adb21f0353d4.tldr: 该工作提出了一种面向长上下文推理的 CPU-GPU 协同混合稀疏注意力方案，在几乎不损失质量的前提下显著提升了推理速度。
arxiv:2605.07719|f8405365322adb21f0353d4.recommendation_reason: 该论文聚焦于长上下文推理中的高效注意力计算、稀疏化策略以及 CPU-GPU 协同加速，这些主题与关注大模型推理优化、稀疏注意力、系统级性能提升和跨设备计算协同的研究方向高度相关。

arxiv:2605.07721|3a202701c4220e1827f6b41.summary_zh: 本文提出了一种面向循环式语言模型的内存高效架构MELT，旨在将推理深度与显存消耗解耦。该方法通过在各次推理循环间共享每层KV缓存，并结合可学习门控机制对缓存进行更新，从而避免显存随迭代次数线性增长。为了稳定训练，作者设计了分块训练的两阶段后训练流程，包括插值过渡和注意力对齐蒸馏。实验表明，MELT在保持循环推理能力的同时，显存占用显著低于基线循环模型，并可取得优于同规模标准语言模型的性能。
arxiv:2605.07721|3a202701c4220e1827f6b41.tldr: MELT通过共享KV缓存实现循环推理的恒定显存开销，同时保持甚至提升循环语言模型的推理性能。
arxiv:2605.07721|3a202701c4220e1827f6b41.recommendation_reason: 该研究聚焦于循环式/递归式语言模型的推理机制、显存效率优化以及多步推理架构设计，与循环推理、长链推理和高效注意力缓存管理等主题高度相关。

arxiv:2605.06675|b2f9be52a915bb327063609.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型推理时 KV cache 线性增长带来的内存瓶颈，研究了 KV cache 量化中的混合精度比特分配问题。作者指出，不同量化器的失真曲线差异很大，若直接沿用其他量化器的模型，会导致比特分配顺序错误，甚至使效果劣于统一量化。为此，论文提出 RateQuant，先用少量校准数据拟合每个量化器的失真模型，再基于率失真理论用闭式解进行反向水填充分配比特。实验表明，该方法在较低平均比特下能显著降低困惑度，并且校准开销很小、推理时无额外代价。
arxiv:2605.06675|b2f9be52a915bb327063609.tldr: RateQuant 通过为 KV cache 量化器单独拟合失真模型并采用率失真理论进行最优比特分配，提升了混合精度量化效果且几乎无推理开销。
arxiv:2605.06675|b2f9be52a915bb327063609.recommendation_reason: 该研究与低比特量化、模型压缩、注意力机制优化以及大语言模型高效推理等主题高度相关，尤其适合关注混合精度分配和量化理论方法的论文推荐。

arxiv:2605.06946|a48b8f18a8df35e3d49463f.summary_zh: 本文针对序列建模中的记忆容量与计算效率权衡问题，改进了 log-linear attention 的记忆衰减机制。作者将原本固定的衰减参数 λ 改为由输入驱动的动态学习方式，并用轻量级两层 MLP 生成逐 token、逐层级的衰减系数。为避免不同层级之间的竞争，方法采用 softplus 进行独立缩放，从而保持原有的 log-linear 复杂度不变。实验表明，该方法在关联记忆、选择性复制和语言建模任务上优于基线，尤其在长程记忆场景中提升更明显。
arxiv:2605.06946|a48b8f18a8df35e3d49463f.tldr: 通过让 log-linear attention 的记忆衰减随输入自适应变化，模型在不增加复杂度的前提下提升了长程记忆能力。
arxiv:2605.06946|a48b8f18a8df35e3d49463f.recommendation_reason: 该研究主题与高效序列建模、长程依赖建模以及注意力机制改进密切相关，适合关注线性/对数线性注意力、记忆压缩和动态门控机制的读者。

arxiv:2605.07783|6f5baf6d7a3c1a18ed30168.summary_zh: 本文提出了一种用于初始化可变尺寸小语言模型的链式蒸馏方法，通过少量中间锚点模型逐步传递大模型知识，从而避免为不同目标规模反复调用大教师模型。该方法先构建稀疏的蒸馏链，再通过相邻锚点之间的参数插值初始化目标模型，提升了训练效率与扩展性。针对异构场景，作者还设计了跨架构、跨词表的桥接蒸馏机制，以支持不同模型设置下的知识迁移。实验结果表明，该方法在效率和下游性能上均优于从零训练的基线，并且适用于多种模型初始化场景。
arxiv:2605.07783|6f5baf6d7a3c1a18ed30168.tldr: 一种通过少量中间锚点和参数插值实现高效、可扩展小语言模型初始化的链式蒸馏方法。
arxiv:2605.07783|6f5baf6d7a3c1a18ed30168.recommendation_reason: 该研究与小语言模型压缩、知识蒸馏、模型初始化以及大模型向小模型迁移知识等主题高度相关，适合关注高效训练与可扩展蒸馏方法的读者。

arxiv:2605.06683|c5e1905603ec51c6c84567d.summary_zh: 本文提出了一种名为 Toeplitz MLP Mixer（TMM）的序列建模架构，用三角掩码的 Toeplitz 矩阵乘法替代注意力机制，以降低 Transformer 类模型的计算复杂度。该方法在训练阶段可实现较低的时间和空间开销，并在推理前填充阶段保持较高效率。实验结果表明，TMM 在相同计算预算下具有更好的训练效率，能够保留更多输入信息，从而提升复制、信息检索和上下文学习等任务表现。作者还从算子指标理论角度分析了 Toeplitz 层的可逆性现象，揭示了训练后模型行为与直觉上的可逆性关系不完全一致。
arxiv:2605.06683|c5e1905603ec51c6c84567d.tldr: TMM 用 Toeplitz 矩阵乘法替代注意力，在降低复杂度的同时提升了信息保留与序列任务性能。
arxiv:2605.06683|c5e1905603ec51c6c84567d.recommendation_reason: 该研究聚焦于高效序列建模、替代注意力机制以及提升信息保留与上下文学习能力，与关注大模型架构优化、低复杂度序列模型和信息检索性能的研究主题具有较高相似性。

arxiv:2605.07182|6c5f9326370c3409f71f425.summary_zh: Star Elastic 提出了一种面向推理型大语言模型的后训练方法，可以在一次训练过程中生成多个嵌套子模型，从而显著降低训练成本。该方法支持在 SSM、Embedding、MoE 和 FFN 等多个结构维度上进行嵌套，并通过端到端可训练路由器与课程式知识蒸馏学习子模型。它进一步引入弹性预算控制，使不同推理阶段可动态选择不同规模的子模型，以适配 token 难度和计算需求。实验表明，该方法在保持或提升精度的同时显著降低延迟，并可扩展到量化场景以减少部署开销。
arxiv:2605.07182|6c5f9326370c3409f71f425.tldr: Star Elastic 通过一次后训练生成多层嵌套推理模型，并支持按阶段动态分配计算预算，以提升精度-延迟权衡。
arxiv:2605.07182|6c5f9326370c3409f71f425.recommendation_reason: 该研究与高效大语言模型压缩、动态推理计算分配、模型族构建以及推理阶段自适应路由等主题高度相关。

arxiv:2605.06763|6f90bb5058549782e2611d6.summary_zh: 本文将稀疏注意力的 KV 缓存检索问题重新表述为半空间范围搜索问题，旨在提升大模型推理效率同时避免遗漏关键 token。作者指出，现有稀疏注意力方法通常依赖固定或自适应预算，难以保证解码过程中零漏召回，尤其在长链路推理任务中更易引发输出误差。为此，论文提出了面向 KV cache 的新型索引结构 Louver，可在给定阈值下实现理论与实践中的零假阴性。实验结果表明，Louver 在准确率和运行时性能上均优于已有稀疏注意力方法，并且在速度上也可超过部分高优化的稠密注意力实现。
arxiv:2605.06763|6f90bb5058549782e2611d6.tldr: 论文通过将稀疏注意力建模为范围搜索问题，提出了可保证零漏召回的高效 KV 缓存索引 Louver。
arxiv:2605.06763|6f90bb5058549782e2611d6.recommendation_reason: 该研究与高效注意力机制、KV 缓存检索、稀疏注意力加速以及大语言模型推理优化等主题高度相关，尤其关注在降低计算开销的同时保持召回与精度。

arxiv:2605.06997|c721ffa0c850d8e45cc6f34.summary_zh: 本文提出了一种无需 KV cache 的关联记忆检索架构 Echo，旨在缓解长序列推理和工具调用场景下 Transformer 线性增长的显存开销。该方法通过 Spectral Koopman Attention 将键值历史压缩为常数内存中的谱动力学统计量，并用闭式算子进行检索。实验表明，在多查询关联回忆任务上，Echo 能在多种间隔和键值对数量配置下达到很高的检索准确率，且显著优于纯状态空间模型及其混合版本。进一步的迁移实验显示，该方法在针尖寻针、多跳检索和工具轨迹等任务上也保持了稳定优势，同时推理内存保持恒定。
arxiv:2605.06997|c721ffa0c850d8e45cc6f34.tldr: Echo 通过谱 Koopman 注意力实现了无 KV cache 的常数内存长程关联检索，并在多种长上下文检索任务上显著优于现有状态空间方法。
arxiv:2605.06997|c721ffa0c850d8e45cc6f34.recommendation_reason: 该研究聚焦于长序列中的高效记忆检索、常数内存推理以及状态空间模型与注意力机制的结合优化，与长上下文建模、检索增强推理和低显存序列模型等主题高度相关。

arxiv:2605.07363|dd54def03df8f31e73c798f.summary_zh: 本文提出了 MISA，一种用于长上下文大语言模型推理的稀疏注意力索引器替代方案。该方法将原本需要大量查询头逐 token 打分的索引器头视作专家池，并通过轻量路由器按查询动态选择少量激活头进行计算，从而显著降低推理成本。为进一步保持选择结果的准确性，论文还设计了层次化变体，在候选集上进行二次重排序以尽量恢复原始索引结果。实验表明，MISA 在多个长上下文基准上可在无需额外训练的情况下接近原始方法表现，并获得明显加速。
arxiv:2605.07363|dd54def03df8f31e73c798f.tldr: MISA 通过动态路由少量索引头来替代密集的多头稀疏注意力索引器，从而在保持效果的同时大幅降低长上下文推理开销。
arxiv:2605.07363|dd54def03df8f31e73c798f.recommendation_reason: 该工作与长上下文大语言模型推理、稀疏注意力机制、注意力加速与高效上下文选择等研究主题高度相关。

arxiv:2605.06982|9c6a31acd82f1c9eabe4015.summary_zh: 该论文提出了 FastOmniTMAE，用于改进基于 Tsetlin Machine 的静态词嵌入训练效率。方法通过将原本顺序依赖的训练流程重构为“评估”和“更新”两个阶段的并行过程，从而提升可扩展性和硬件执行效率。在分类任务上，训练速度最高可提升 5 倍，同时在相似度相关指标上保持与原方法相近的嵌入质量。作者还将其实现为适用于 SoC-FPGA 的可复用加速器，展示了在资源受限硬件上的良好表现。
arxiv:2605.06982|9c6a31acd82f1c9eabe4015.tldr: FastOmniTMAE 通过并行化 Tsetlin 嵌入训练流程，实现了更快的训练速度和更适合硬件部署的逻辑式词嵌入。
arxiv:2605.06982|9c6a31acd82f1c9eabe4015.recommendation_reason: 该研究聚焦于高效词嵌入、NLP 表示学习以及模型训练加速，与关注文本表示方法、嵌入训练效率和硬件友好机器学习的主题具有较强相似性。

arxiv:2605.07111|15971cb1e9c2d02e62ecc6f.summary_zh: 这篇论文讨论了大语言模型微调中全参数微调与LoRA各自的优势与局限，并指出仅依赖静态方案在不同任务上存在结构性限制。作者基于SQL、医疗问答和反事实知识注入等任务进行了系统评测，验证了两种方法在不同场景下的互补性。为此，论文提出MoLF框架，在优化器层面动态路由更新到全参数与LoRA之间，使训练过程中两个专家都能获得准确梯度信号。实验表明，MoLF在多数设置下可达到或超过两类基线中的较优结果，而MoLF-Efficient在受限显存条件下也表现出更强的自适应微调能力。
arxiv:2605.07111|15971cb1e9c2d02e62ecc6f.tldr: 论文提出一种在全参数微调与LoRA之间动态路由梯度更新的统一框架，以提升大语言模型适配的稳定性和效果。
arxiv:2605.07111|15971cb1e9c2d02e62ecc6f.recommendation_reason: 该研究聚焦于大语言模型参数高效微调、全参数微调与LoRA的比较及动态自适应路由，与关注模型微调策略、训练效率和任务适配性能的研究主题高度相关。

arxiv:2605.08044|3777d512ad3317f326b3162.summary_zh: 这篇论文提出了用于字节级语言模型的加速生成方法，旨在缓解逐字节自回归解码带来的速度瓶颈。作者在 Byte Latent Transformer 基础上提出了 BLT Diffusion，并结合块级扩散目标与标准下一字节预测训练，从而支持一次并行生成多个字节。论文还提出了 BLT Self-speculation 和 BLT Diffusion+Verification 两种变体，以在速度与生成质量之间取得不同平衡。实验表明，这些方法在生成任务上可显著降低前向传播次数，并将内存带宽成本降低超过 50%。
arxiv:2605.08044|3777d512ad3317f326b3162.tldr: 该论文通过扩散式并行生成和投机式验证机制显著加速了字节级语言模型的推理。
arxiv:2605.08044|3777d512ad3317f326b3162.recommendation_reason: 该研究聚焦于字节级语言模型的高效生成、推理加速与质量权衡，适合关注大模型解码优化、低开销生成和语言模型架构改进的相关主题。

arxiv:2605.07488|04b13f0714d45ba90c37633.summary_zh: 本文提出了一种面向多模态模型的数据选择框架 One-Step-Train（OST），将数据筛选重写为增量优化效用排序问题。该方法不依赖语义启发式规则，而是通过轻量代理模型的一步模拟更新来估计每个样本的边际贡献。实验结果表明，OST 在多模态数学推理基准上能够以更低训练成本获得更优性能，并实现帕累托最优效率。与此同时，该方法还能识别有害样本，缓解噪声数据带来的负迁移问题。
arxiv:2605.07488|04b13f0714d45ba90c37633.tldr: OST 通过估计样本的边际优化价值来进行数据筛选，在降低训练成本的同时提升了多模态模型的推理性能。
arxiv:2605.07488|04b13f0714d45ba90c37633.recommendation_reason: 该研究聚焦于多模态模型的数据筛选、样本效用评估与训练效率优化，适合关注大模型数据选择、低成本训练和多模态推理性能提升的相关主题。

arxiv:2605.07315|86e52f50bc31a8a82cf6472.summary_zh: 本文提出 LaTER，一种用于大模型测试时推理的两阶段框架，先在连续潜空间中进行有限探索，再切换到显式链式思维进行验证与作答。该方法旨在减少传统 CoT 推理带来的高 token 开销，同时尽量保留符号检查能力。作者给出了无需训练的实现方式，并利用熵与停止 token 探针来判断何时切换阶段。实验表明，该方法在多个基准上可显著降低 token 使用量，并在部分任务上保持甚至提升准确率；进一步的监督微调还能带来更强的性能提升。
arxiv:2605.07315|86e52f50bc31a8a82cf6472.tldr: LaTER 通过“先潜空间探索、后显式验证”的两阶段推理方式，在减少 token 开销的同时提升或保持大模型推理性能。
arxiv:2605.07315|86e52f50bc31a8a82cf6472.recommendation_reason: 该研究聚焦于大语言模型推理效率提升、链式思维压缩、隐式表示与显式验证结合等主题，与高效推理和模型推理成本优化方向高度相关。

arxiv:2605.07750|2ef374170b99df1a88755c6.summary_zh: 本文面向大规模多核加速器的快速而精确的端到端建模问题，重点解决周期精确 RTL 仿真过慢以及延迟敏感互连行为难以准确估计的挑战。作者针对采用紧耦合 scratchpad memory 的 many-core 架构，提出了一种能够刻画跨不同互连规模下 SPM 访问时序的建模方法，同时抽象掉非关键硬件细节。实验表明，该方法在多种基准上相较 cycle-accurate RTL 金模型误差低于 7%，同时仿真速度最高提升 115 倍。该框架还支持对处理单元与互连进行细粒度 profiling，便于软件优化和硬件设计空间探索。
arxiv:2605.07750|2ef374170b99df1a88755c6.tldr: 本文提出了一种面向延迟敏感 many-core 架构的快速精确建模方法，可在保持较高精度的同时大幅加速端到端仿真。
arxiv:2605.07750|2ef374170b99df1a88755c6.recommendation_reason: 该研究与多核/众核系统建模、片上互连性能分析、时序敏感仿真加速以及存储层次与 NoC 协同设计等主题高度相关，适合关注体系结构建模与设计空间探索的读者。

arxiv:2605.07248|85092eca5c0ced402ea26af.summary_zh: 该论文提出了一种用于测试时代码生成的自适应计算策略 PaT（Planning-after-Trial）。与传统先规划后尝试的方式不同，PaT 先进行生成与验证，只有在验证失败后才调用规划器，从而避免在简单问题上浪费规划开销。该方法还支持异构模型配置，让低成本模型负责初始生成，高能力模型仅在需要时介入规划。实验结果表明，PaT 在多个基准和模型家族上都能显著改善成本与性能的平衡，并在接近大模型效果的同时大幅降低推理成本。
arxiv:2605.07248|85092eca5c0ced402ea26af.tldr: PaT 通过“先尝试、后规划”的自适应策略提升了测试时代码生成的效率，并显著降低推理成本。
arxiv:2605.07248|85092eca5c0ced402ea26af.recommendation_reason: 该研究聚焦于大语言模型的测试时计算优化、自适应推理策略以及代码生成效率提升，和关注推理阶段计算分配、模型协同与成本性能权衡的研究主题高度相关。

arxiv:2605.06878|600add1a4dbf566aa1ea3e3.summary_zh: 本文提出了一种面向深度学习推理的运行时自适应、多精度向量引擎，利用 CORDIC 迭代深度与计算精度之间的关系，实现近似与精确执行模式的动态切换。该架构将低资源的迭代式 CORDIC MAC 单元与时分复用的多激活函数模块结合，支持 8/16 位灵活精度并提高硬件利用率。ASIC 实现结果表明，该方法在计算周期和功耗方面都有明显优化，同时保持较高的算力密度与能效。FPGA 验证也显示其能够在低功耗条件下完成实时目标检测推理。
arxiv:2605.06878|600add1a4dbf566aa1ea3e3.tldr: 该工作通过 CORDIC 加速和多精度自适应设计，提升了深度学习推理的能效与硬件利用率。
arxiv:2605.06878|600add1a4dbf566aa1ea3e3.recommendation_reason: 该研究与深度学习推理加速、低功耗硬件设计、多精度计算以及面向边缘设备的高能效神经网络部署等主题高度相关。

arxiv:2605.08317|8c7d4627965e3a959a5afe4.summary_zh: 该研究针对大语言模型长上下文推理中的 KV cache 内存与带宽瓶颈，提出将 cache 压缩统一建模为率失真优化问题。作者认为 eviction 和 quantization 本质上是同一比特分配机制的两个极端，因此需要联合优化。基于注意力计算引入的失真权重，方法为 token 或 channel 分配不同位宽，并通过 reverse water-filling 在预填充阶段一次性完成压缩。实验表明，该方法在多个长上下文基准上优于现有方案，并能在较小缓存保留率下维持接近全量缓存的效果。
arxiv:2605.08317|8c7d4627965e3a959a5afe4.tldr: 提出一种将 KV cache 的淘汰与量化统一为率失真比特分配的联合压缩方法，以更高效支持长上下文推理。
arxiv:2605.08317|8c7d4627965e3a959a5afe4.recommendation_reason: 该论文与长上下文大语言模型推理优化、KV cache 压缩、内存带宽瓶颈缓解以及量化/淘汰联合策略等研究主题高度相关。

arxiv:2605.10453|365637eeddec7ad7120b092.summary_zh: 本文提出了 SlimSpec，一种用于 speculative decoding 的低秩 draft LM-head 参数化方法，用于加速大语言模型的自回归生成。该方法通过压缩中间表示而不是裁剪词表，保留了完整词表支持，从而避免了额外的词表筛选与复杂推理逻辑。实验基于 EAGLE-3 drafter 和多个目标模型、多个基准展开，覆盖了不同的延迟受限与吞吐受限场景。结果显示，SlimSpec 相比标准 LM-head 可带来约 4 到 5 倍加速，并保持具有竞争力的接受长度。整体上，该方法在训练和推理流程上改动较小，适合作为多种 draft LM-head 架构的高效替代方案。
arxiv:2605.10453|365637eeddec7ad7120b092.tldr: SlimSpec 通过对 draft LM-head 做低秩压缩，在保留完整词表的同时显著加速 speculative decoding。
arxiv:2605.10453|365637eeddec7ad7120b092.recommendation_reason: 该研究聚焦于大语言模型推理加速、speculative decoding、draft 模型设计以及输出层计算优化，与高效生成、模型压缩和低开销推理等主题高度相关。

arxiv:2605.09490|518841aaff80b2b994b54c1.summary_zh: 本文面向大模型推理过程中的长链式思维缓存占用问题，提出一种语义感知的分层内存管理方法，将 token 分配到 HBM、DDR、压缩和驱逐四个层级。与直接丢弃低重要性 token 不同，该方法优先将低重要性 token 转移到 CPU 内存，并在注意力计算前按需预取回 GPU，从而实现零近似误差的卸载。实验表明，推理准确率主要取决于被永久丢弃的 token 比例，而不是 HBM 中保留了多少 token。该方法在多个模型规模和基准上能够显著降低 HBM 占用，同时保持较高的推理性能，且数据传输开销较小。
arxiv:2605.09490|518841aaff80b2b994b54c1.tldr: 提出一种语义感知的 LLM 推理内存分层机制，用 CPU 内存替代直接驱逐低重要性 token，以在减少 HBM 占用的同时尽量保持推理准确率。
arxiv:2605.09490|518841aaff80b2b994b54c1.recommendation_reason: 该研究聚焦于大模型推理中的 KV cache 管理、内存层次优化与长上下文推理效率提升，与关注 LLM 资源优化、推理加速和显存/内存协同管理的主题高度相关。

arxiv:2605.08696|4b433729fdfc1f1937b6dbc.summary_zh: 本文提出了一种结构化循环混合器（Structured Recurrent Mixer）架构，能够在训练时采用序列并行表示，并在推理时代数转换为循环表示。该设计在无需专用内核或设备特定内存管理的情况下，同时兼顾了训练效率与推理吞吐。实验结果表明，该方法相比其他线性复杂度模型具有更高的信息容量、更强的并发能力和更好的推理性能。作者还展示了该架构在强化学习训练中的有效性。
arxiv:2605.08696|4b433729fdfc1f1937b6dbc.tldr: 该工作提出一种可在训练与推理间灵活切换表示的混合架构，以提升语言序列生成的效率、吞吐与并发能力。
arxiv:2605.08696|4b433729fdfc1f1937b6dbc.recommendation_reason: 该论文与序列建模、语言模型架构优化、高效推理以及大规模并行生成等研究主题高度相关，适合关注高效神经网络与长序列处理的读者。

arxiv:2605.10875|3bc6e56b1e8bdb8ea2dbc37.summary_zh: 本文提出了自优化语言模型（SOL）框架，用于在自回归解码过程中按 token 动态分配计算预算。该方法在冻结大模型参数的前提下，引入轻量策略网络，根据隐藏状态为每个生成步骤选择不同的效率动作。可选动作同时覆盖注意力稀疏、MLP 结构化激活剪枝和激活量化比特宽度，从而实现细粒度的推理加速控制。实验表明，SOL 在相同预算下优于静态分配和强随机搜索，并能获得更优的质量-效率帕累托前沿，在 MMLU 上最高提升 7.3%。
arxiv:2605.10875|3bc6e56b1e8bdb8ea2dbc37.tldr: 该工作通过按 token 动态调整推理计算开销，在不改动基座模型权重的情况下显著提升了大语言模型的效率与准确性。
arxiv:2605.10875|3bc6e56b1e8bdb8ea2dbc37.recommendation_reason: 该研究聚焦于大语言模型推理效率优化、动态计算预算分配以及量化、剪枝和稀疏注意力等压缩/加速技术，与语言模型高效推理和资源自适应调度方向高度相关。

arxiv:2605.09463|31ac0a7010f55d9403fe537.summary_zh: 本文关注大语言模型在长上下文场景中的计算开销和信息冗余问题，提出了一种将上下文压缩从位置驱动转向语义驱动的方法。该方法通过选择与查询相关的语义中心，并以一致性加权方式合并其他 token，减少了传统软提示压缩中的位置偏置。实验在两个基础模型的14个基准上验证了该方法在下游任务表现、推理延迟和域外鲁棒性方面的优势。整体上，该研究强调通过语义一致性来提升长上下文压缩的稳定性与有效性。
arxiv:2605.09463|31ac0a7010f55d9403fe537.tldr: 该工作提出一种语义驱动的上下文压缩方法，以减少位置偏置并提升长上下文处理效果。
arxiv:2605.09463|31ac0a7010f55d9403fe537.recommendation_reason: 该论文与长上下文处理、上下文压缩、语义表示建模以及提升大语言模型推理效率等研究主题高度相关。

arxiv:2605.08840|8104e8c0c300b3513c49c1d.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型在长序列生成推理中 KV cache 内存开销不断增大的问题，提出了一种更稳健的 KV 缓存淘汰方法 ReST-KV。该方法不再仅依赖注意力权重，而是通过层级输出重构来直接衡量移除 token 对模型输出的影响，从而更好地刻画注意力重分配效应。为提升淘汰决策的稳定性，方法进一步引入指数滑动平均平滑以处理时间变化，并结合自适应窗口机制捕捉空间模式。实验表明，该方法在多个长上下文基准上均取得了显著提升，并能大幅降低解码延迟。
arxiv:2605.08840|8104e8c0c300b3513c49c1d.tldr: ReST-KV 通过层级输出重构与时空平滑实现更鲁棒的 KV cache 淘汰，显著提升长上下文推理效率与性能。
arxiv:2605.08840|8104e8c0c300b3513c49c1d.recommendation_reason: 该研究主题与大模型长上下文推理、KV cache 压缩与淘汰策略、以及提升生成效率和鲁棒性的方向高度相关。

arxiv:2605.08134|303eef22929de7cc5a3ecb7.summary_zh: 本文针对扩散式大语言模型在推理效率方面的瓶颈，提出利用注意力激活复用来减少冗余计算。作者观察到双向自注意力中存在明显的 token 级冗余，并利用查询表示的时序变化来预测相关的键、值和输出激活是否可复用。基于这一发现，论文设计了 DARE-KV 和 DARE-O 两种互补机制，分别复用 KV 激活与输出激活。实验表明，该方法在几乎不损失生成质量的前提下，可显著降低延迟并提升推理效率。
arxiv:2605.08134|303eef22929de7cc5a3ecb7.tldr: DARE 通过复用扩散式大语言模型中的注意力激活，减少冗余计算并提升推理效率，且几乎不影响性能。
arxiv:2605.08134|303eef22929de7cc5a3ecb7.recommendation_reason: 该工作与高效大模型推理、注意力机制优化以及生成模型加速等研究主题高度相关，适合关注模型推理加速和计算复用方法的读者。

arxiv:2605.09877|0fda3d77ca09baa8ba301ca.summary_zh: 本文提出了一种新的注意力块递归机制 Key-Value Means（KVM），可支持固定大小或可增长状态。将其用于强 Transformer 基线后，可以在仅增加极少参数的情况下实现高效的 O(N) 分块 RNN 形式。进一步地，带有可增长 KVM 缓存的模型在长上下文测试中表现具有竞争力，同时保持次二次预填充时间和次线性状态增长。该方法还可用标准算子实现，无需自定义内核，并支持分块并行训练与预填充。
arxiv:2605.09877|0fda3d77ca09baa8ba301ca.tldr: KVM 提供了一种统一的注意力递归方案，在长上下文建模中兼顾线性计算、可扩展记忆和高效并行。
arxiv:2605.09877|0fda3d77ca09baa8ba301ca.recommendation_reason: 该研究与长上下文建模、注意力机制改进、线性或次二次复杂度序列建模以及高效记忆压缩等方向具有较强主题相似性。

arxiv:2605.09649|bb5fd960d46585723aa80b4.summary_zh: 这篇论文关注长上下文推理中的 KV cache 内存与计算瓶颈问题。作者指出，传统的全量缓存并不一定最优，因为无关 token 可能会稀释模型对关键信息的注意力。为此，论文提出一种基于全局保留策略的可学习 KV eviction 方法，通过轻量级保留门控和统一的评分投影来估计 token 的未来价值。实验表明，该方法在多种长上下文语言、视觉语言推理和多轮对话任务中，可以显著降低 KV 内存占用，同时达到或超过全量缓存推理效果。
arxiv:2605.09649|bb5fd960d46585723aa80b4.tldr: 该论文提出一种全局可学习的 KV cache 剔除方法，在减少长上下文内存开销的同时还能提升或保持推理性能。
arxiv:2605.09649|bb5fd960d46585723aa80b4.recommendation_reason: 该研究与长上下文建模、缓存压缩、推理效率优化以及基于选择性保留的重要信息筛选方法高度相关，适合关注大模型长序列推理性能提升的读者。

arxiv:2605.08301|b17e85ea94029dc5f5fd3f4.summary_zh: 本文提出了 Priming 方法，用于将混合状态空间模型（Hybrid SSM）从预训练 Transformer 中初始化并快速迁移。通过短暂的对齐与后训练阶段，模型能够以极少的预训练 token 成本恢复下游性能，同时保持更小的 KV cache 和更高的解码吞吐。作者还在统一条件下对多种 SSM 层类型进行了规模化比较，发现其表达能力层级能够直接预测长上下文推理任务表现。实验表明，该方法可扩展到 8B/32B 级推理模型，并在长上下文能力与效率之间取得良好平衡。
arxiv:2605.08301|b17e85ea94029dc5f5fd3f4.tldr: Priming 让混合 SSM 模型从预训练 Transformer 快速迁移，并在长上下文推理上兼顾性能与推理效率。
arxiv:2605.08301|b17e85ea94029dc5f5fd3f4.recommendation_reason: 该研究聚焦于混合状态空间模型、长上下文建模、推理效率提升以及从 Transformer 向新架构的知识迁移，与关注高效序列建模和大模型架构演进的主题高度相关。

arxiv:2605.09008|e29fd5b058654f683b46beb.summary_zh: 本文针对大语言模型在链式思维推理场景中的推理开销和KV缓存内存瓶颈，研究了结构化剪枝在高稀疏率下导致推理能力退化的问题。作者指出，基于幅值的传统剪枝方法容易偏向高频但信息量较低的语法性特征，从而引发推理崩塌。为此，论文提出了 Relative Kinetic Utility（RKU）框架，将离散剪枝转化为沿模型深度的连续动力学积分，并结合 Fisher trace 归一化以识别关键的高曲率逻辑通路。实验表明，该方法在约 40% 稀疏率下仍能较好保持推理性能，并在多个模型与分布外评测中表现出更强的推理表示保留能力。
arxiv:2605.09008|e29fd5b058654f683b46beb.tldr: 本文提出一种面向推理的结构化剪枝方法 RKU，以在高稀疏率下更好保留大语言模型的推理能力。
arxiv:2605.09008|e29fd5b058654f683b46beb.recommendation_reason: 该研究与大语言模型推理效率提升、结构化剪枝、稀疏化压缩以及推理能力保持等主题高度相关，适合关注模型压缩与推理优化方向的读者。

arxiv:2605.09735|e39a593d8e605b4f6b892f8.summary_zh: 本文研究静态图 LLM 服务中 KV-cache 管理带来的运行时不稳定问题，指出在线解码时请求长度变化、EOS 异步到达和历史片段化会导致内存浪费与尾延迟抖动。作者提出 KV-RM 运行时设计，在固定解码接口下对 KV-cache 迁移进行规整，通过逻辑历史与物理存储解耦、块分页跟踪和单次提交描述符来支持更稳定的执行。其还采用合并式传输路径，将非连续 KV 映射聚合为少量大传输组，再由固定形状注意力核消费。实验表明，该方法在混合长度解码场景下提升吞吐与尾延迟表现，减少预留 KV 内存，并显著缓解生产轨迹下的突发延迟尖峰。
arxiv:2605.09735|e39a593d8e605b4f6b892f8.tldr: KV-RM 通过规整 KV-cache 迁移，在不改变静态图解码接口的前提下提升了 LLM 服务的吞吐、内存效率与尾延迟稳定性。
arxiv:2605.09735|e39a593d8e605b4f6b892f8.recommendation_reason: 该研究聚焦于大模型推理服务中的 KV-cache 管理、静态图执行优化、运行时调度与低延迟推理，与关注高效 LLM serving、缓存管理和系统性能优化的研究主题高度相关。

arxiv:2605.09176|dceb35936b58bec9c990dbf.summary_zh: 这篇综述从系统与优化的视角梳理了大语言模型训练中的优化器设计，覆盖了经典一阶方法、自适应优化、节省内存的变体、二阶与曲率感知方法、符号更新、低秩投影以及矩阵式优化器等方向。文章指出，随着模型规模不断扩大，优化器研究已不再只关注单次速度提升，而是同时权衡收敛性、稳定性、内存占用和实现复杂度。作者还重点讨论了大规模训练中的基准评测问题，包括超参数公平性、尺度依赖性、墙钟时间、token 效率和下游效果。整体上，论文强调未来需要更严格、可比较、面向规模的优化器评估框架。
arxiv:2605.09176|dceb35936b58bec9c990dbf.tldr: 这是一篇面向大语言模型训练优化器的综述，系统总结了从 AdamW 到内存高效和矩阵式优化方法的发展与评测标准。
arxiv:2605.09176|dceb35936b58bec9c990dbf.recommendation_reason: 该论文与大模型训练优化、参数更新策略、内存效率以及优化算法比较评测等研究主题高度相关，适合关注高效训练方法与优化器设计的读者。

arxiv:2605.10886|e8671e64f5e592d3e6dd285.summary_zh: 本文提出了 LoKA 框架，用于在大规模推荐模型中更有效地应用低精度计算，尤其是 FP8。研究指出，推荐模型对数值精度更敏感，且其计算模式与大语言模型不同，因此直接使用 FP8 往往会损害模型质量并延长训练时间。LoKA 通过系统与模型协同设计，结合真实分布下的统计分析、模型组件改造以及运行时调度，提升低精度推理和训练的可行性。实验设计强调根据不同层的误差和安全性动态选择合适的 FP8 内核，以在精度要求与性能收益之间取得平衡。
arxiv:2605.10886|e8671e64f5e592d3e6dd285.tldr: LoKA 通过统计分析、模型改造和运行时调度，让 FP8 在大规模推荐模型中更稳定、更高效地落地。
arxiv:2605.10886|e8671e64f5e592d3e6dd285.recommendation_reason: 该研究聚焦于大规模推荐模型中的低精度计算优化、数值稳定性与系统-模型协同设计，与推荐系统加速、模型压缩和高性能训练等主题具有较强相似性。

arxiv:2605.08894|134dc2d63225c3f219db24b.summary_zh: 本文研究了极低比特量化对大语言模型带来的额外退化现象，指出问题不仅仅是前向计算的数值误差，还包括模型输出平滑性的系统性下降。作者通过平滑性代理指标和序列邻域建模发现，随着量化位宽降低，模型在预测邻域中的有效候选词迅速减少，从而使解码树更稀疏、生成质量变差。为此，论文提出一种保持平滑性的简单原则，并将其应用于后训练量化和量化感知训练中。实验表明，在保证数值精度之外，维护平滑性还能进一步提升极端量化模型的效果。
arxiv:2605.08894|134dc2d63225c3f219db24b.tldr: 论文指出极低比特量化会损害LLM的输出平滑性，并提出保持平滑性的量化原则以改善生成质量。
arxiv:2605.08894|134dc2d63225c3f219db24b.recommendation_reason: 该研究聚焦于大语言模型量化压缩中的性能退化机理，尤其关注极端低比特量化对模型生成质量和稳健性的影响，与模型压缩、量化优化及高效部署方向高度相关。

arxiv:2605.09932|7911a02e6dbf9467393cc51.summary_zh: 本文提出了 FocuSFT，一种用于长上下文监督微调的双层优化框架，旨在缓解训练过程中注意力被位置偏置和 attention sink 稀释的问题。作者指出，长序列中的内容 token 往往得不到充分关注，从而削弱梯度信号并限制模型学习稳健长上下文能力。FocuSFT 通过内循环自适应轻量 fast-weight 参数，构建更聚焦相关内容的参数化记忆，再由外循环在此基础上进行微调。实验表明，该方法在多个长上下文基准上显著提升性能，并明显减少训练中的注意力 sink 现象。
arxiv:2605.09932|7911a02e6dbf9467393cc51.tldr: FocuSFT 通过双层优化在训练时聚焦长上下文中的关键信息，显著提升大模型的长文本理解与使用能力。
arxiv:2605.09932|7911a02e6dbf9467393cc51.recommendation_reason: 该研究聚焦于长上下文建模、监督微调优化、注意力机制改进以及提升模型对远距离语义信息的利用能力，与长文本理解和长序列训练优化方向高度相关。

arxiv:2605.08755|5b288632869d10e92b300f0.summary_zh: 本文针对大推理模型在长链式解码场景下量化后性能下降的问题，分析了现有端到端量化训练在推理基准上失效的原因。作者从梯度方向、KV-cache 保真度以及校准数据与部署分布的 Hessian 子空间对齐等角度，解释了困扰长推理量化的关键因素。为此，提出了一种无需在线转换开销的逐层权重量化方法 LAQuant，通过一层前瞻损失和推理领域校准来保持跨层协同与残差流质量。实验表明，该方法在低比特量化下能够同时提升数学推理精度并获得较好的解码加速效果。
arxiv:2605.08755|5b288632869d10e92b300f0.tldr: LAQuant 通过逐层前瞻损失和推理域校准，提升了长推理模型低比特量化后的精度与速度。
arxiv:2605.08755|5b288632869d10e92b300f0.recommendation_reason: 该研究聚焦于大模型推理场景中的量化压缩、低比特权重训练以及长链式解码下的性能保持，与关注模型压缩、推理加速和量化感知训练的主题高度相关。

arxiv:2605.09100|86a0d3f6df799c455cf66f5.summary_zh: 本文提出了一种统一框架 GRC，旨在将推理驱动生成、文本表示学习和上下文压缩整合到一次前向传播中完成。作者通过元潜在 token 和统一的生成、表征与压缩调优方法，让模型能够同时服务于生成、检索嵌入和压缩三类任务。该框架在推理增强的检索、文档压缩和 RAG 场景中表现出较好的效果，同时降低了训练与部署成本。研究还引入了新的文本嵌入与记忆式生成范式，为长上下文和持续学习提供了新的实现思路。
arxiv:2605.09100|86a0d3f6df799c455cf66f5.tldr: GRC 通过统一训练与推理机制，把推理生成、检索表征和上下文压缩整合为一个高效框架。

arxiv:2605.08234|4034a1811217fe1cc315642.summary_zh: 这篇论文关注长上下文大模型推理中的 KV cache 压缩问题，指出仅看任务准确率不足以判断选择器为何成功或失败。作者提出了一种固定契约诊断方法，通过固定选择器设置并逐项改变决策槽位，来分析证据恢复、输出价值排序和相关证据保留这三个关键环节。论文进一步结合注意力质量与移除块后的输出变化，构造用于价值排序的探针。实验表明，该方法在 LongBench、NeedleBench 和 RULER 上能较好区分支持恢复与价值排序等不同效应，并为缓存压缩策略提供了更清晰的诊断顺序。
arxiv:2605.08234|4034a1811217fe1cc315642.tldr: 本文提出固定契约诊断框架，用于分析值感知 KV 淘汰在长上下文压缩中的失效原因，并指导更有效的缓存保留策略。

arxiv:2605.11186|213385e9c4aec7ba624cbd1.tldr: Auto-regressive decoding in Large Language Models (LLMs) is inherently memory-bound: every generation step requires loading the model weights and intermediate results from memory (e.g., High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) for GPU servers), making throughput bottlenecked by memory bandwidth rather than compute. Speculative decoding addresses this by enabling parallel verification of multiple draft tokens, effectively amortizing the cost of each target-model call. However, existing speculative decoding methods are designed under the assumption that HBM is sufficiently large to hold both the target model and an auxiliary draft model simultaneously -- an assumption that breaks down on memory-constrained devices such as edge platforms with limited DRAM. We analyze the inference bottleneck in this memory-limited regime and propose CATS, a self-speculative decoding framework that conducts cascaded verification and correction based on the memory budget and parameter offloading patterns on memory-limited devices. This design maximizes token acceptance rate and end-to-end speedup while keeping the peak memory footprint on the device equal to that of the target model alone. We evaluate CATS on different models across five benchmarks on real edge devices. CATS can achieve a wall-clock speedup of up to 5.08x with no degradation in generation quality, outperforming the SOTA method by up to 1.45x under edge memory constraints.

arxiv:2605.11744|d73b942128d20fa247ddeac.tldr: Transformer-based large language models face severe scalability challenges in long-context generation due to the computational and memory costs of full-context attention. Under practical computation and memory constraints, many inference-efficient long-context methods improve efficiency by adopting bounded-context or segment-level execution only during inference, while continuing to train models under full-context attention, resulting in a mismatch between training and inference execution and state-transition semantics. Based on this insight, we propose a training-inference consistent segment-level generation framework, in which training and inference follow the same segment-level forward execution semantics. During training, consistency with inference is enforced by restricting gradient propagation to KV states carried over from the immediately preceding segment, while permitting head-specific access to past KV states during the forward pass without involving them in gradient propagation. Across long-context benchmarks, our approach achieves performance comparable to full-context attention, while achieving competitive latency-memory trade-offs against strong inference-efficient baselines, and substantially improving scalability at very long context lengths (e.g., approximately 6x lower peak prefill memory at 128K compared to full-context attention with FlashAttention).

arxiv:2605.11581|70af7ba8a46ab53fbb36fd1.tldr: When large language models (LLMs) serve real-time inference in commercial online advertising systems, end-to-end latency must be strictly bounded to the millisecond range. Yet every token generated during the decode phase triggers thousands of kernel launches, and kernel launch overhead alone can account for 14.6% of end-to-end inference time. MegaKernel eliminates launch overhead and inter-operator HBM round-trips by fusing multiple operators into a single persistent kernel. However, existing MegaKernel implementations face a fundamental tension between portability and efficiency on resource-constrained GPUs such as NVIDIA Ada: hand-tuned solutions are tightly coupled to specific architectures and lack portability, while auto-compiled approaches introduce runtime dynamic scheduling whose branch penalties are unacceptable in latency-critical settings. We observe that under a fixed deployment configuration, the optimal execution path of a MegaKernel is uniquely determined, and runtime dynamic decision-making can be entirely hoisted to compile time. Building on this insight, we propose Ada-MK: (1) a three-dimensional shared-memory constraint model combined with K-dimension splitting that reduces peak shared memory usage by 50%; (2) MLIR-based fine-grained DAG offline search that solidifies the optimal execution path, completely eliminating runtime branching; and (3) a heterogeneous hybrid inference engine that embeds MegaKernel as a plugin into TensorRT-LLM, combining high-throughput Prefill with low-latency Decode. On an NVIDIA L20, Ada-MK improves single-batch throughput by up to 23.6% over vanilla TensorRT-LLM and 50.2% over vLLM, achieving positive gains across all tested scenarios--the first industrial deployment of MegaKernel in a commercial online advertising system.

arxiv:2605.12471|fc4adfa30d0fbaa753c0bd4.tldr: We introduce KV-Fold, a simple, training-free long-context inference protocol that treats the key-value (KV) cache as the accumulator in a left fold over sequence chunks. At each step, the model processes the next chunk conditioned on the accumulated cache, appends the newly produced keys and values, and passes the enlarged cache forward; the same one-step update is applied repeatedly, analogous to foldl in functional programming. Building on the KV cache concatenation primitive introduced for latent multi-agent communication, we repurpose it as a chunk-to-chunk recurrence for long-context inference. When processing chunk t, the model attends to the KV cache carried from earlier chunks as a prefix, reusing its internal state across segments without modifying or retraining the model. Despite its simplicity, the induced recurrence is stable: per-step drift rises briefly and then saturates into a flat plateau that persists across deep chains. This plateau is insensitive to a 10,000x change in numerical precision, robust across chunk sizes, and consistent across model families. At the task level, KV-Fold preserves exact information over long distances. On a needle-in-a-haystack benchmark, it achieves 100% exact-match retrieval across 152 trials spanning contexts from 16K to 128K tokens and chain depths up to 511 on Llama-3.1-8B, while remaining within the memory limits of a single 40GB GPU. Compared to streaming methods, which trade fidelity for bounded memory, KV-Fold maintains long-range retrieval while operating as a sequence of tractable forward passes. Overall, our results show that frozen pretrained transformers already support a stable form of KV-cache recurrence, providing a practical route to long-context inference without architectural changes or training.

arxiv:2605.12357|98882078631809311cc468a.tldr: Large language models increasingly need to accumulate and reuse historical information in long-term assistants and agent systems. Simply expanding the context window is costly and often fails to ensure effective context utilization. We propose $δ$-mem, a lightweight memory mechanism that augments a frozen full-attention backbone with a compact online state of associative memory. $δ$-mem compresses past information into a fixed-size state matrix updated by delta-rule learning, and uses its readout to generate low-rank corrections to the backbone's attention computation during generation. With only an $8\times8$ online memory state, $δ$-mem improves the average score to $1.10\times$ that of the frozen backbone and $1.15\times$ that of the strongest non-$δ$-mem memory baseline. It achieves larger gains on memory-heavy benchmarks, reaching $1.31\times$ on MemoryAgentBench and $1.20\times$ on LoCoMo, while largely preserving general capabilities. These results show that effective memory can be realized through a compact online state directly coupled with attention computation, without full fine-tuning, backbone replacement, or explicit context extension.

arxiv:2605.11537|76189ba0759da2b821c09bf.tldr: The Mixture of Experts (MoE) architecture has become a fundamental building block in state-of-the-art large language models (LLMs), improving domain-specific expertise in LLMs and scaling model capacity without proportionally increasing their computational overhead. However, MoE inference often suffers from suboptimal GPU utilization, load imbalance, and elevated latency arising from multiple tokens waiting on the same experts for their computation which arises from sparsity of expert activation. To address these challenges, we propose a dynamic expert replication strategy that predicts which experts are likely to be overloaded and replicates them for upcoming batches of tokens. The replicated experts process batch tokens concurrently across layers, which leads to improved parallelism, shorter GPU idle time, and significantly faster inference. Experimental evaluations conducted on large-scale MoE models, including Switch-base-128 and Switch-base-256, demonstrate that our method achieves near-complete GPU utilization (approx 100%), leading to upto 3x improvement in inference speed while preserving approximately 90-95% of the performance of baseline architectures

arxiv:2605.11577|f2b57eabe1c85838e987aee.tldr: Autoregressive language models generate text one token at a time, yet natural language is inherently structured in multi-token units, including phrases, n-grams, and collocations that carry meaning jointly. This one-token bottleneck limits both the expressiveness of the model during pre-training and its throughput at inference time. Existing remedies such as speculative decoding or diffusion-based language models either leave the underlying bottleneck intact or sacrifice the causal structure essential to language modeling. We propose BitLM, a language model that represents each token as a fixed-length binary code and employs a lightweight diffusion head to denoise multiple tokens in parallel within each block. Crucially, BitLM preserves left-to-right causal attention across blocks while making joint lexical decisions within each block, combining the reliability of autoregressive modeling with the parallelism of iterative refinement. By replacing the large-vocabulary softmax with bitwise denoising, BitLM reframes token generation as iterative commitment in a compact binary space, enabling more efficient pre-training and substantially faster inference without altering the causal foundation that makes language models effective. Our results demonstrate that the one-token-at-a-time paradigm is not a fundamental requirement but an interface choice, and that changing it can yield a stronger and faster language model. We hope BitLM points toward a promising direction for next-generation language model architectures.

arxiv:2605.11678|d0069088ea39f83d0a13185.tldr: End-to-end Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models for autonomous driving unify perception, reasoning, and control in a single neural network, achieving strong driving performance but requiring 20-60GB of GPU memory-far exceeding the 12-16GB available on commodity GPUs. We present a framework, which enables memory-efficient VLA inference on VRAM-constrained GPUs through system-level optimization alone, without model modification. Our work proceeds in three stages: (1) Sequential Demand Layering reduces VRAM usage from model-level to layer-level granularity; (2) Pipelined Demand Layering hides parameter transfer time within layer execution time via transfer--compute overlap; and (3) a GPU-Resident Layer Decision Policy, informed by per-module residency benefit analysis, eliminates the residual transfer overhead that pipelining cannot hide. We further propose a performance prediction model that determines the optimal configuration-both the number and placement of resident layers-from a single profiling run with less than 1.3% prediction error across all configurations. Applied to NVIDIA's Alpamayo-R1-10B (21.52GB) on an RTX 5070Ti (16GB), our work achieves up to 3.55x speedup over Accelerate offloading while maintaining full BF16 precision.

arxiv:2605.12464|5174fc16b8f9e08c852f346.tldr: Quantization has emerged as a standard technique for accelerating inference for generative models by enabling faster low-precision computations and reduced memory transfers. Recently, GPU accelerators have added first-class support for microscaling Block Floating Point (BFP) formats. Standard BFP algorithms use a fixed scale based on the maximum magnitude of the block. We observe that this scale choice can be suboptimal with respect to quantization errors. In this work, we propose ScaleSearch, an alternative strategy for selecting these scale factors: using a fine-grained search leveraging the mantissa bits in microscaling formats to minimize the quantization error for the given distribution. ScaleSearch can be integrated with existing quantization methods such as Post Training Quantization and low-precision attention, and is shown to improve their performance. Additionally, we introduce ScaleSearchAttention, an accelerated NVFP4-based attention algorithm, which uses ScaleSearch and adapted prior techniques to ensure near-0 performance loss for causal language modeling. Experiments show that ScaleSearch reduces quantization error by 27% for NVFP4 and improves language model PTQ by up to 15 points for MATH500 (Qwen3-8B), while ScaleSearchAttention improves Wikitext-2 PPL by upto 0.77 points for Llama 3.1 70B. The proposed methods closely match baseline performance while providing quantization accuracy improvements.

arxiv:2605.11222|91f0848a96980f4b82c2b69.tldr: Quantization is an effective strategy to reduce the storage and computation footprint of large language models (LLMs). Post-training quantization (PTQ) is a leading approach for compressing LLMs. Popular weight quantization procedures, including GPTQ and RTN, suffer in model utility, especially at aggressive quantization levels (sub-4-bit). We propose ADMM-Q, a novel weight quantization algorithm that considers the layer-wise quantization problem. Our algorithm is based on a combinatorial variant of the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM). Our operator-splitting procedure updates weights continuously to minimize the layer-wise reconstruction error, while gradually enforcing the quantization constraints with convergence guarantees. We propose additional algorithmic enhancements (e.g., penalty scheduling, preconditioning, and a local search post-processing step) to make ADMM-Q efficient at LLM scale. ADMM-Q is modular and can be used as a drop-in replacement for any weight quantizer within existing quantization pipelines: ADMM-Q is fully composable with existing techniques including range clipping, learned or random rotations, and activation scaling. Using ADMM-Q in place of GPTQ on Qwen3-8B, we decrease WikiText-2 perplexity in: (i) the W3A16 weight-only setting (12.85 $\rightarrow$ 10.06); (ii) the W4A8 SmoothQuant procedure (9.29 $\rightarrow$ 8.68); and (iii) the W2A4KV4 SpinQuant procedure (66.11 $\rightarrow$ 19.42).

arxiv:2605.11277|25cf7e208569792b440cd84.tldr:
Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) has become a dominant architecture for scaling large language models (LLMs). However, the execution characteristics of MoE inference are changing rapidly and increasingly mismatch the assumptions underlying existing Processing-in-Memory (PIM) systems. Prior PIM systems for LLMs rely on static rules to offload memory-bound operations to PIM, without accounting for the combined effects of load imbalance and inter-GPU communication. Meanwhile, modern MoE models activate fewer experts out of increasingly many, creating a bimodal expert distribution: a small set of experts receives many tokens, while a long tail of experts receives only one or a few.
  We identify a trend in modern MoE models toward increasingly bimodal token-to-expert distributions, quantify the resulting disparity in arithmetic intensity across experts, and show that this disparity dramatically reduces the efficiency of state-of-the-art PIM systems for LLMs. To address this problem, we propose a scheduler for serving MoE models on multi-GPU systems with attached HBM-PIM stacks. Our scheduler partitions expert execution between GPU and PIM based on runtime token-to-expert distributions, while jointly considering interconnect overhead, memory bandwidth, GPU throughput, and PIM throughput. Moreover, we propose Sieve, a runtime framework that employs the scheduler to coordinate execution across GPUs and their attached HBM-PIM stacks. Sieve overlaps GPU computation, PIM computation, and intra- and inter-device communication while preserving cross-device dependencies induced by expert parallelism. Sieve is evaluated on our cycle-accurate simulator based on Ramulator 2.0. Compared to state-of-the-art PIM systems for MoE, Sieve improves both throughput and interactivity by 1.3x, 1.3x, and 1.6x on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B, GPT-OSS-120B, and Qwen3-30B-A3B, respectively.

arxiv:2605.12260|c7f065e4e3f93d7745b8fa3.tldr: Long-horizon language agents accumulate conversation history far faster than any fixed context window can hold, making memory management critical to both answer accuracy and serving cost. Existing approaches either expand the context window without addressing what is retrieved, perform heavy ingestion-time fact extraction at substantial token cost, or rely on heuristic graph traversal that leaves both accuracy and efficiency on the table. We present PRISM, a training-free retrieval-side framework that treats long-horizon memory as a joint retrieval-and-compression problem over a graph-structured memory. PRISM combines four orthogonal inference-time components: Hierarchical Bundle Search over typed relation paths, Query-Sensitive Edge Costing that aligns traversal with detected query intent, Evidence Compression that compresses the candidate bundle into a compact answer-side context, and Adaptive Intent Routing that routes most queries through zero-LLM tiers. By formulating retrieval as min-cost selection over typed path templates and pairing it with an LLM-side compression step, PRISM surfaces the right evidence under a strict context budget without any fine-tuning or modification to the upstream ingestion pipeline. Experiments on the LoCoMo benchmark show that PRISM delivers substantially higher LLM-judge accuracy than every same-protocol baseline at an order-of-magnitude smaller context budget, occupying a previously empty corner of the accuracy-context-cost frontier and demonstrating a superior balance between answer quality and retrieval efficiency.

arxiv:2605.11005|2e5301893dcf82fe403ebf3.tldr: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) architectures enable trillion-parameter LLMs with sparsely activated experts. Expert parallelism (EP) is a widely adopted MoE training strategy, but it suffers from severe all-to-all communication bottlenecks, which is exaggerated by the limited inter-node network bandwidth as the growing model size requires distributing experts across GPU nodes. Prior work focused on overlapping these all-to-all communications with feed-forward network (FFN) and self-attention computations, which often leaves residual network-bound stalls due to inherent imbalance in attention and FFN layers' computation-communication ratios. We present DisagMoE, a disaggregated MoE training system that jointly optimizes model placement and scheduling for maximal efficiency. DisagMoE separates attention and FFN layers into disjoint GPU groups, introduces a multi-stage pipeline with uni-directional, many-to-many communications, and employs a computation-communication roofline model to balance GPU and network bandwidth allocation among the attention and FFN groups. DisagMoE is implemented on Megatron-LM, and evaluation shows that DisagMoE improves training efficiency across multiple MoE models with up to 1.8x speedup on 16-node 8xH800 clusters.

arxiv:2605.11093|eb38f0be9e4c9cefea1f164.tldr: Today's inference-time workloads increasingly depend on timely access to a model's internal states. We present DMI-Lib, a high-speed deep model inspector that treats internal observability as a first-class systems primitive, decoupling it from the inference hot path via an asynchronous observability substrate built from Ring^2, a GPU-CPU memory abstraction for capturing and staging tensors, and a policy-controlled host backend that exports them. DMI-Lib enables the placement of observation points across a rich space of internal signals and diverse inference backends while preserving serving optimizations and adhering to tight GPU memory budgets. Our experiments demonstrate that DMI-Lib incurs only 0.4%--6.8% overhead in offline batch inference and an average of 6% in moderate online serving, reducing latency overhead by 2x-15x compared to existing baselines with similar observability features. DMI-Lib is open-sourced at https://github.com/ProjectDMX/DMI.

arxiv:2605.11800|0201f14311b4dfe051e155f.tldr: Large language models (LLMs) with mixture-of-experts (MoE) architectures achieve remarkable scalability by sparsely activating a subset of experts per token, yet their frequent expert switching creates memory bandwidth bottlenecks that compute-in-memory (CIM) architectures are well-suited to mitigate. However, analog CIM systems suffer from inherent hardware imperfections that perturb stored weights, and its negative impact on MoE-based LLMs in noisy CIM environments remains unexplored. In this work, we present the first systematic investigation of MoE-based LLMs under noise model calibrated with real chip measurements, revealing that hardware noise critically disrupts expert load balance and renders clean-trained routing decisions consistently suboptimal. Based on these findings, we propose ROMER, a post-training calibration framework that (1) replaces underactivated experts with high-frequency ones to restore load balance, and (2) recalibrates router logits via percentile-based normalization to stabilize routing under noise. Extensive experiments across multiple benchmarks demonstrate that ROMER achieves up to 58.6\%, 58.8\%, and 59.8\% reduction in perplexity under real-chip noise conditions for DeepSeek-MoE, Qwen-MoE, and OLMoE, respectively, establishing its effectiveness and generalizability across diverse MoE architectures.

arxiv:2605.12245|38454495caa334c3c162d4e.tldr: NVFP4 has recently emerged as an efficient 4-bit microscaling format for large language models (LLMs), offering superior numerical fidelity with native hardware support. However, existing methods often yield suboptimal performance due to inflexible scale selection and the coupled treatment of quantization and dequantization scales. To address these issues, we propose Scale Optimization for Accurate Reconstruction (SOAR), a novel post-training quantization framework that improves the accuracy of NVFP4 quantization. At its core, SOAR features Closed-form Joint Scale Optimization (CJSO), which jointly optimizes global and block-wise scales via analytical solutions derived from reconstruction error minimization. Furthermore, it incorporates Decoupled Scale Search (DSS). DSS decouples the high-precision quantization scale from its constrained dequantization counterpart, and performs discrete search to mitigate precision loss from scale quantization. Extensive experiments across multiple LLMs show that our method consistently outperforms existing NVFP4 quantization baselines, achieving superior accuracy under the same memory footprint with no additional hardware overhead. The code and models will be available at https://github.com/steven-bao1/SOAR.

arxiv:2605.12466|a2bbd9377270a43422269c8.tldr: Looped Transformers offer a promising alternative to purely feed-forward computation by iteratively refining latent representations, improving language modeling and reasoning. Yet recurrent architectures remain unstable to train, costly to optimize and deploy, and constrained to small, fixed recurrence depths. We introduce Attractor Models, in which a backbone module first proposes output embeddings, then an attractor module refines them by solving for the fixed point, with gradients obtained through implicit differentiation. Thus, training memory remains constant in effective depth, and iterations are chosen adaptively by convergence. Empirically, Attractor Models outperform existing models across two regimes, large-scale language-model pretraining and reasoning with tiny models. In language modeling, Attractor Models deliver a Pareto improvement over standard Transformers and stable looped models across sizes, improving perplexity by up to 46.6% and downstream accuracy by up to 19.7% while reducing training cost. Notably, a 770M Attractor Model outperforms a 1.3B Transformer trained on twice as many tokens. On challenging reasoning tasks, we show that our model with only 27M parameters and approximately 1000 examples achieves 91.4% accuracy on Sudoku-Extreme and 93.1% on Maze-Hard, scaling favorably where frontier models like Claude and GPT o3, fail completely, and specialized recursive reasoners collapse at larger sizes. Lastly, we show that Attractor Models exhibit a novel phenomenon, which we call equilibrium internalization: fixed-point training places the model's initial output embedding near equilibrium, allowing the solver to be removed at inference time with little degradation. Together, these results suggest that Attractor Models make iterative refinement scalable by turning recurrence into a computation the model can learn to internalize.

arxiv:2605.11196|f912a9c0086eda13bb23088.tldr: Linear attention reduces the quadratic cost of softmax attention to $\mathcal{O}(T)$, but its memory state grows as $\mathcal{O}(T)$ in Frobenius norm, causing progressive interference between stored associations. We introduce \textbf{Variational Linear Attention} (VLA), which reframes the memory update as an online regularised least-squares problem with an adaptive penalty matrix maintained via the Sherman-Morrison rank-1 formula. We prove that normalising the write direction to unit length gives the recurrence Jacobian spectral norm exactly $1$ for all sequence lengths and head dimensions (Proposition 2), and that the state norm is self-limiting under bounded inputs (Proposition 1). Empirically, VLA reduces $\|S_t\|_F$ by $109\times$ relative to standard linear attention at $T{=}1{,}000$, achieves near-perfect exact-match accuracy on multi-query associative recall within the effective per-head memory regime ($n_\text{pairs} < d_h$), maintaining substantially higher retrieval performance than DeltaNet and standard linear attention under increasing memory load, and maintains 62\% accuracy at the per-head capacity boundary. A Triton-fused kernel achieves $14\times$ speedup over sequential Python and $\mathcal{O}(T)$ scaling, crossing below softmax attention latency at approximately 43\,000 tokens.

arxiv:2605.11374|033b1a02a81219ca97dadaf.tldr: Test-time compute is widely believed to benefit only large reasoning models. We show it also helps small embedding models. Most modern embedding checkpoints are distilled from large LLM backbones and inherit their representation space; a frozen embedding model should therefore benefit from extra inference compute without retraining. Using an agentic program-search loop, we explore 259 candidate inference programs over a frozen embedding API across ninety generations. The entire Pareto frontier collapses onto a single algebra: a softmax-weighted centroid of the local top-K documents interpolated with the query. This parameter-free default lifts nDCG@10 statistically significantly across seven embedding-model families spanning a tenfold parameter range, with held-out full-BEIR validation confirming the lift on every model tested.

arxiv:2605.11603|1a3bb6a65a53aacd89ef0c1.tldr: The growing deployment of large language models (LLMs) makes per-request routing essential for balancing response quality and computational cost across heterogeneous model pools. Current routing methods rarely consider sustainable energy use and CO2 emissions as optimization objectives, despite grid carbon intensity varying by time and region, and models differing significantly in energy consumption. To address this gap, we introduce Green-Aware Routing (GAR), a constrained multi-objective optimization framework that minimizes per-request CO2 emissions subject to explicit accuracy floors and p95-latency service-level objectives (SLOs). GAR employs adaptive constraint optimization through per-dataset floor tuning and incorporates lightweight estimators for correctness, tail latency, and carbon emissions, enabling real-time routing decisions without additional inference passes. We present GAR-PD, a practical online primal-dual routing algorithm for rolling carbon budgets, alongside heuristic variants that achieve high feasibility coverage while limiting accuracy degradation. Comprehensive experiments across standard NLP benchmarks with heterogeneous LLM pools (7B-70B) demonstrate that GAR achieves substantial carbon reductions while maintaining competitive accuracy and p95 latency guarantees, providing a practical, theoretically grounded approach to sustainable LLM inference.

arxiv:2605.12825|bcc038bf58cf5f9a6738180.tldr: We introduce Orthrus, a simple and efficient dual-architecture framework that unifies the exact generation fidelity of autoregressive Large Language Models (LLMs) with the high-speed parallel token generation of diffusion models. The sequential nature of standard autoregressive decoding represents a fundamental bottleneck for high-throughput inference. While diffusion language models attempt to break this barrier via parallel generation, they suffer from significant performance degradation, high training costs, and a lack of rigorous convergence guarantees. Orthrus resolves this dichotomy natively. Designed to seamlessly integrate into existing Transformers, the framework augments a frozen LLM with a lightweight, trainable module to create a parallel diffusion view alongside the standard autoregressive view. In this unified system, both views attend to the exact same high-fidelity Key-Value (KV) cache; the autoregressive head executes context pre-filling to construct accurate KV representations, while the diffusion head executes parallel generation. By employing an exact consensus mechanism between the two views, Orthrus guarantees lossless inference, delivering up to a 7.8x speedup with only an O(1) memory cache overhead and minimal parameter additions.

arxiv:2605.13190|55e50b68eabe79469f54045.tldr: Improving the inference efficiency of autoregressive transformers typically means reducing FLOPs per token, usually through approximations that degrade model quality. We introduce N-vium, a mixture-of-exits transformer that partially parallelizes computation across depth on standard hardware, increasing effective FLOPs per second rather than minimizing compute per token. N-vium attaches prediction heads at multiple depths and defines the next-token distribution as a learned mixture over these exits, with token-adaptive routing. This formulation strictly generalizes the standard transformer, which is recovered exactly when routing assigns zero mass to all intermediate heads. Sampling from the mixture is exact, and complete KV caches are recovered by deferring the upper-layer computation and batching it with later tokens. We pretrain N-vium at scales up to 1.5B parameters. Our largest model reaches 57.9% wall-clock speedup over a parameter- and data-matched standard transformer at no perplexity cost.

arxiv:2605.13784|881cc36c56a4630730905ac.tldr: Conventional transformer inference engines are request-driven, paying an O(n) prefill cost on every query. In streaming workloads, where data arrives continuously and queries probe an ever-growing context, this cost is prohibitive. We introduce a data-driven computational model centred on stateful sessions: a persistent KV cache advanced incrementally as new data arrives, so prefill is moved off the critical path and query latency becomes O(|q|), independent of accumulated context size. Building on this, Flash Queries reclaim idle GPU cycles between data arrivals to pre-evaluate registered questions and return cached answers before the user asks, a pattern that is structurally impossible in stateless engines because they discard intermediate state between requests. A multi-tenant continuous-batching scheduler with cell-budget admission and prefix-aware grouped prefill lets dozens of stateful sessions coexist on a single GPU while preserving full quadratic self-attention. On streaming market-data benchmarks the reference implementation achieves up to 5.9x speedup over conventional inference engines (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, llama.cpp), holding query latency constant as accumulated context grows.

arxiv:2605.13162|e32e1ad550abfac6b2b7e18.tldr: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT), particularly Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), has become a standard approach for adapting Large Language Models (LLMs) under limited compute. However, in continual settings where models are updated sequentially with small datasets, conventional LoRA updates struggle to balance rapid adaptation and knowledge retention. Existing methods typically treat the low-rank space as a homogeneous update region, lacking mechanisms to regulate how short-term updates are consolidated over time. We propose a continual LoRA framework with \textbf{Pro}gram memory, inspired by \textbf{C}omplementary \textbf{L}earning Systems in neuroscience. Our approach, dubbed \textbf{ProCL}, organizes LoRA adapters into structured program memory slots that are dynamically retrieved through input-conditioned attention. This enables rapid and localized adaptation, encouraging similar inputs to reuse shared adapter regions while reserving unused capacity for future data. The slots are then combined with the underlying adapter, which maintains a distributed representation that gradually accumulates knowledge across tasks to balance plasticity and stability. Our method operates entirely within the LoRA parameterization and incurs no additional inference cost. Experiments on diverse benchmarks demonstrate improved retention and reduced catastrophic forgetting over other continual LoRA strategies.

arxiv:2605.13370|c877b151e006d2cebfbcdbe.tldr: For over a decade, explicit memory architectures like the Neural Turing Machine have remained theoretically appealing yet practically intractable for language modeling due to catastrophic gradient instability during Backpropagation Through Time. In this work, we break this stalemate with \textit{Phasor Memory Network} (PMNet), a novel architecture that structurally resolves memory volatility through \textit{Unitary Phasor Dynamics} and \textit{Hierarchical Learnable Anchors}. Rather than relying on brute-force scaling, we present a mechanistic proof-of-concept in a controlled byte-level setting. By constraining recurrent state updates to phase rotations on a complex unit circle, PMNet preserves gradient norms and inherently prevents divergence without the need for specialized initialization. We empirically demonstrate the active actuation of the memory module through a synthetic Copy-Paste task, where PMNet utilizes an expansive \textit{85-slot hierarchical memory tree} ($=\sum^{4}_{h=1}4^{h-1}$) to achieve near 100\% exact retrieval across temporal distances that completely exceed the local sliding window attention's receptive field. Furthermore, despite being a compact 119M parameter model trained on 18.8B tokens, PMNet matches the zero-shot long-context robustness of a Mamba model that is three times larger. Our ablation studies and gradient analyses confirm that the historical failure of explicit memory was a structural alignment problem, which PMNet effectively overcomes, providing a theoretically grounded foundation for scalable sequence modeling.

arxiv:2605.13779|a454f904eb91bbd1ee64087.tldr: We present MindLab Toolkit (MinT), a managed infrastructure system for Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) post-training and online serving. MinT targets a setting where many trained policies are produced over a small number of expensive base-model deployments. Instead of materializing each policy as a merged full checkpoint, MinT keeps the base model resident and moves exported LoRA adapter revisions through rollout, update, export, evaluation, serving, and rollback, hiding distributed training, serving, scheduling, and data movement behind a service interface. MinT scales this path along three axes. Scale Up extends LoRA RL to frontier-scale dense and MoE architectures, including MLA and DSA attention paths, with training and serving validated beyond 1T total parameters. Scale Down moves only the exported LoRA adapter, which can be under 1% of base-model size in rank-1 settings; adapter-only handoff reduces the measured step by 18.3x on a 4B dense model and 2.85x on a 30B MoE, while concurrent multi-policy GRPO shortens wall time by 1.77x and 1.45x without raising peak memory. Scale Out separates durable policy addressability from CPU/GPU working sets: a tensor-parallel deployment supports 10^6-scale addressable catalogs (measured single-engine sweeps through 100K) and thousand-adapter active waves at cluster scale, with cold loading treated as scheduled service work and packed MoE LoRA tensors improving live engine loading by 8.5-8.7x. MinT thus manages million-scale LoRA policy catalogs while training and serving selected adapter revisions over shared 1T-class base models.

arxiv:2605.12879|d08de8b1f37bff590a729fc.tldr: Doubly-stochastic attention has emerged as a transport-based alternative to row-softmax attention, with recent Transformer variants using it to reduce attention sinks and rank collapse while improving performance. In this family, the standard approach is Sinkhorn scaling, which trains more efficiently but still repeats matrix scaling in every inference forward pass. Sliced-transport attention removes the online iteration, but its soft sorting approximation materializes dense tensors for each slice, requiring substantially more training resources than Sinkhorn attention. We introduce ASAP: Amortized Doubly-Stochastic Attention via Sliced Dual Projection, a train-then-compile method that trains the doubly-stochastic layer with Sinkhorn, then replaces the iterative scaling loop at inference with a fixed sliced-dual operator. It learns a lightweight parametric map from exact one-dimensional Kantorovich potentials to the Sinkhorn query-side dual, then reconstructs the attention plan with a two-sided entropic c-transform. Across language and vision benchmarks, ASAP keeps the cheaper training setup and remains highly competitive with recent baselines. In the main frozen-layer benchmark, ASAP is 5.3 faster than the trained Sinkhorn teacher while matching its accuracy; in downstream replacements, ASAP recovers most of the teacher performance without any retraining.

arxiv:2605.12928|5c4bd24c8a21b47d96dfd07.tldr: Modern language models have historically relied on two dominant design choices: subword tokenization and autoregressive (AR) ordering. These design decisions bake in priors that dictate a model's learning. Recently, two alternative paradigms have challenged this: byte-level modeling, which bypasses static statistically-derived token vocabularies, and masked diffusion modeling (MDM), which conducts parallel, non-sequential generation. Their intersection represents a fully end-to-end modality-agnostic generative prototype; however, removing these structural priors incurs a significant computational cost. In this work, we investigate this cost through a compute-matched scaling study. Our results reveal that the performance penalty of byte modeling is not uniform; across scale, the scaling overhead of byte modeling is worse for MDM than for AR. We hypothesize that this disparity stems from context fragility: while AR's stable causal history allows models to naturally rediscover subword patterns, the MDM objective destroys the local contiguity required to efficiently resolve semantics from raw bytes. Our findings from controlled permutation experiments suggest that future modality-agnostic designs must incorporate alternative structural biases to maintain viable scaling trajectories in the byte regime.

arXiv:2605.13429v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Tokenization is a foundational step in the text process of Large Language Models (LLMs). Texts must be first tokenized into token IDs, which are then input to LLMs. Inefficient tokenization results in long token-ID sequences and will slow down the training and inference of LLMs. The fine-grained knowledge transfer between LLMs, like token-level distillation, is also impeded by the mismatch in vocabulary. To bridge this gap, we introduce a method named TokAlign++ to improve vocabulary adaptation performance by learning better token alignment lexicon. The source and target vocabularies are taken as two different languages, and the bilingual token alignment lexicon is learned from monolingual token representations. Model parameters are rearranged following this bilingual lexicon for new vocabulary, and progressively fine-tuned for adaptation. Experimental results on 15 languages show that our method boosts the multilingual text compression rates and preserves most of the multilingual ability of vanilla models. It costs as few as 1k steps to restore the performance of the vanilla model. After unifying vocabularies between vanilla models, token-level distillation remarkably improves the base model with only 235M tokens.

arxiv:2605.13833|591a933d5a30f832282daa9.tldr: Modeling long-range dependencies in sequential data remains a central challenge in machine learning. Transformers address this challenge through attention mechanisms, but their quadratic complexity with respect to sequence length limits scalability to long contexts. State-space models (SSMs) provide an efficient alternative with linear-time computation by evolving a latent state through recurrent updates, but their memory is typically formed via additive or linear transitions, which can limit their ability to capture complex global interactions across tokens. In this work, we introduce one of the first studies to leverage the superposition property of quantum systems to enhance state-based sequence modeling. In particular, we propose Quantum Long-Attention Memory (QLAM), a hybrid quantum-classical memory mechanism that can be viewed as a quantum extension of state-space models. Instead of maintaining a classical latent state updated through additive dynamics, QLAM represents the hidden state as a quantum state whose amplitudes encode a superposition of historical information. The state evolves through parameterized quantum circuits conditioned on the input, enabling a non-classical, globally update mechanism. In this way, QLAM preserves the recurrent and linear-time structure of SSMs while fundamentally enriching the memory representation through quantum superposition. Unlike attention mechanisms that explicitly compute pairwise interactions, QLAM implicitly captures global dependencies through the evolution of the quantum state, and retrieves task-relevant information via query-dependent measurements. We evaluate QLAM on sequential variants of standard image classification benchmarks, including sMNIST, sFashion-MNIST, and sCIFAR-10, where images are flattened into token sequences. Across all tasks, QLAM consistently improves over recurrent baselines and transformer-based models.

arxiv:2605.13247|d74a9cfcbb9f0c5ae4fb467.tldr: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models offer a powerful way to scale model size without increasing compute, as per-token FLOPs depend only on k active experts rather than the total pool of E experts. Yet, this asymmetry creates an MoE efficiency paradox in practice: adding more experts balloons memory and communication costs, making actual training inefficient. We argue that this bottleneck arises in part because current MoE training allocates too many experts from the beginning, even though early-stage data may not fully utilize such capacity. Motivated by this, we propose EMO, a simple progressive training framework that treats MoE capacity as expandable memory and grows the expert pool over the course of training. EMO explicitly models sparsity in scaling law to derive stage-wise compute-optimal token budgets for progressive expansion. Empirical results show that EMO matches the performance of a fixed-expert setup in large-scale experiments while improving wall-clock efficiency. It offers a surprisingly simple yet effective path to scalable MoE training, preserving the benefits of large expert pools while reducing both training time and GPU cost.

arxiv:2605.13026|a414fefa4a761cf1eac71db.tldr: Masked diffusion models (MDMs) have emerged as a promising alternative to autoregressive models (ARMs) for language modeling. However, MDMs are known to learn substantially more slowly than ARMs, which may become problematic when scaling MDMs to larger models. Therefore, we ask the following question: how can we accelerate standard MDM training while maintaining its final performance? To this end, we first provide a detailed analysis of why MDM training is slow. We find that the main factor is the locality bias of language: the predictive information for a token is concentrated in nearby positions. We further investigate how this bias slows learning and suggest a simple yet effective remedy: bell-shaped time sampling as a training strategy. Notably, MDMs trained with our training recipe reach the same validation negative log-likelihood (NLL) up to $\sim4\times$ faster than standard training on One Billion Word Benchmark (LM1B). We also show faster improvements in generative perplexity, zero-shot perplexity, and downstream task performance on various benchmarks.

arxiv:2605.13769|a817bad18805060d8eb4179.tldr: We study dense and mixture-of-experts (MoE) transformers in a tiny-scale pretraining regime under a shared LLaMA-style decoder training recipe. The sparse model replaces dense feed-forward blocks with Mixtral-style routed experts. Dense baselines are modestly width-resized to tightly match either active or total parameter budgets, while tokenizer, data, optimizer, schedule, depth, context length, normalization style, and evaluation protocol are held fixed. Our best sparse recipe uses four experts, top-2 routing, Switch-style load balancing, and router z-loss. In a three-seed full-data comparison, the dense active-match model reaches 1.6545 +/- 0.0012 best validation loss, the MoE reaches 1.5788 +/- 0.0020, and the dense total-match model reaches 1.5608 +/- 0.0025. This yields a matched-active gap of 0.0758 +/- 0.0021 in the MoE's favor and a matched-total gap of 0.0180 +/- 0.0020 in the dense model's favor. Across training, the matched-active advantage grows while the matched-total dense advantage narrows sharply. In this sub-25M-parameter regime, MoE therefore improves validation loss under active-parameter matching but does not surpass dense training at equal total stored capacity.

arxiv:2605.12765|25d60f0beb1b54e37d35e42.tldr: Large Language Models memorize vast amounts of training data, raising concerns regarding privacy, copyright infringement, and safety. Machine unlearning seeks to remove the influence of a targeted forget set while preserving model performance, ideally approximating a model retrained from scratch without the forget set. Existing approaches aim to achieve this by updating model parameters via gradient-based methods. However, these updates are computationally expensive, lead to irreversible weight changes, and degrade when the model is quantized for deployment. A recent alternative to changing model weights is activation engineering, where activations are changed during inference to steer model behavior. Despite circumventing weight editing, naive activation steering introduces its own failure modes, as a single global steering vector applies the same intervention to every input, leading to unintended changes in model behavior. We introduce Inference-Time Unlearning via Gated Activation Redirection (GUARD-IT), a training- and gradient-free method that unlearns via input-dependent activation steering at inference time. The resulting intervention is applied as a norm-preserving rotation in the residual stream, leaving model weights untouched. Experiments on TOFU and MUSE show that GUARD-IT matches or exceeds 12 gradient-based baselines across three model scales, while being the only method to simultaneously preserve utility, suppress memorization, and avoid catastrophic collapse across all settings. GUARD-IT further supports continual unlearning without retraining, and remains effective under quantization, a scenario in which parameter-editing methods degrade.
